#!/bin/bash
# Deploy a ref (default: main from /opt/nxeon) to the staging environment —
# without breaking the running staging app while it builds.
#
#   scripts/deploy-staging.sh [git-ref] [--dry-run] [--install-units]
#
# Same release model as promote-production.sh (see scripts/lib/seamless-release.sh):
# the build runs in /tank/nxeon-deploy/staging/build (a worktree of the
# /opt/nxeon-staging repo at origin/<ref>, with staging's .env), the finished
# .next becomes a release under /tank/nxeon-deploy/staging/releases/, gets a
# side-port smoke test (127.0.0.1:3096), then /opt/nxeon-staging/.next (a
# symlink) is swapped atomically and nxeon-staging-web restarted + health-checked
# (auto-rollback on failure). Only after that is /opt/nxeon-staging's own
# source reset to the deployed commit (the staging worker runs from it), deps
# installed, Prisma client generated, the seed run and the worker restarted.
#
# Staging keeps its old schema semantics: `prisma db push --accept-data-loss`.
# Rollback: scripts/rollback-release.sh --staging [RELEASE_ID]
set -euo pipefail

REF=main; DRY_RUN=0; INSTALL_UNITS=0
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    --install-units) INSTALL_UNITS=1 ;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,19p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    -*) echo "unknown option: $a" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    *) REF="$a" ;;
  esac
done
case "$REF" in *[!A-Za-z0-9._/-]*|-*|"") echo "invalid ref: $REF" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac

LIBDIR="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/lib"
source "$LIBDIR/seamless-env-staging.sh"
# shellcheck source=lib/seamless-release.sh
source "$LIBDIR/seamless-release.sh"

hook_schema() {
  [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ] && { log "Schema push skipped (dry run)"; return 0; }
  local dburl; dburl=$(db_url_of_env_file "$APP_DIR/.env")
  log "Applying database schema to '$EXPECT_DB'"
  (cd "$BUILD_DIR" && clean_env DATABASE_URL="$dburl" npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss --skip-generate \
     --schema="$BUILD_DIR/prisma/schema.prisma" 2>&1 | tail -2)
}

hook_after_web() {
  log "Syncing $APP_DIR source to ${TARGET_COMMIT:0:10} (the staging worker runs from it)"
  git -C "$APP_DIR" reset -q --hard "$TARGET_COMMIT"
  install_and_generate "$APP_DIR"
  (cd "$APP_DIR" && clean_env npm run db:seed 2>&1 | tail -2) || true
  chmod 600 "$APP_DIR/.env" 2>/dev/null || true
  check_units "$APP_DIR"
  log "Restarting $WORKER_SERVICE"
  systemctl restart "$WORKER_SERVICE"
  sleep 5
  systemctl is-active "$WEB_SERVICE" "$WORKER_SERVICE" || warn "$WORKER_SERVICE is not active — check journalctl -u $WORKER_SERVICE"
  log "Staging: http://$(grep ^PUBLIC_IP "$APP_DIR/.env" | cut -d= -f2):8080"
}

log "Fetching origin in $REPO_DIR"
git -C "$REPO_DIR" fetch -q origin
TARGET_COMMIT=$(git -C "$REPO_DIR" rev-parse --verify "origin/$REF^{commit}")
run_release_pipeline "$TARGET_COMMIT"
#!/bin/bash
# Promote /opt/nxeon's committed HEAD to production — SEAMLESSLY.
#
#   scripts/promote-production.sh [--dry-run] [--accept-data-loss] [--install-units]
#                                 [--skip-staging-check] [--allow-dirty]
#
# The build NEVER happens in /opt/nxeon any more (that is what took the site
# half-down for 10-12 minutes per promote until 2026-10-01). Instead:
#   1. a git worktree of HEAD at /tank/nxeon-deploy/production/build (ZFS pool;
#      the root disk is ~90% full) with production's .env copied in, its own
#      node_modules and its own Prisma client;
#   2. schema push to the production DB (additive by default — see below);
#   3. `next build` there under nice/ionice, with a stall/overall timeout,
#      holding the box-wide build lock;
#   4. all the old post-build steps (public/ + .next/static + geoip data into
#      standalone, standalone/.env = production .env, chown for 'nxeon');
#   5. the finished .next becomes /tank/nxeon-deploy/production/releases/<id>/;
#   6. that release is booted on 127.0.0.1:3095 and smoke-tested first;
#   7. /opt/nxeon/.next (a SYMLINK to the live release) is swapped in one
#      atomic rename, nxeon-web restarted (downtime = the restart), and
#      /, a real /_next/static chunk, this build's _buildManifest.js and /login
#      must answer 200 — otherwise it AUTO-ROLLS BACK to the previous release;
#   8. only then: npm install + prisma generate in /opt/nxeon for the worker,
#      wait for in-flight PROVISION jobs (max 4 min), restart nxeon-worker;
#   9. keeps the current + 3 previous releases. Rollback any time:
#      scripts/rollback-release.sh --production [RELEASE_ID]
#
# Flags:
#   --dry-run             build + stage + smoke-test only. No schema push (prints
#                         the SQL a push would run), no swap, no restarts.
#   --accept-data-loss    pass --accept-data-loss to `prisma db push`. Without
#                         it, a schema change Prisma flags as possibly
#                         destructive aborts the promote BEFORE anything changes
#                         (the old script always passed it).
#   --install-units       install changed deploy/*.service|*.timer into
#                         /etc/systemd/system + daemon-reload (default: print
#                         the diff command and the install command only).
#   --skip-staging-check  don't require staging to be up and 200.
#   --allow-dirty         build even though /opt/nxeon has uncommitted changes
#                         to TRACKED files (they are NOT included — only the
#                         committed HEAD is built).
set -euo pipefail

DRY_RUN=0; ACCEPT_DATA_LOSS=0; INSTALL_UNITS=0; SKIP_STAGING_CHECK=0; ALLOW_DIRTY=0
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    --accept-data-loss) ACCEPT_DATA_LOSS=1 ;;
    --install-units) INSTALL_UNITS=1 ;;
    --skip-staging-check) SKIP_STAGING_CHECK=1 ;;
    --allow-dirty) ALLOW_DIRTY=1 ;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,42p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "unknown option: $a (see --help)" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

LIBDIR="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/lib"
source "$LIBDIR/seamless-env-production.sh"
# shellcheck source=lib/seamless-release.sh
source "$LIBDIR/seamless-release.sh"

hook_preflight() {
  if [ "$SKIP_STAGING_CHECK" != 1 ]; then
    systemctl is-active -q nxeon-staging-web || die "Refusing to promote: staging web service is not running (--skip-staging-check to override)."
    local code; code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 15 http://127.0.0.1:8080/ || true)
    [ "$code" = 200 ] || die "Refusing to promote: staging returns HTTP $code (--skip-staging-check to override)."
    log "Staging is at $(git -C /opt/nxeon-staging rev-parse --short HEAD) and answers 200"
  fi
  local dirty; dirty=$(git -C "$APP_DIR" status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)
  if [ -n "$dirty" ]; then
    echo "$dirty" | head -20 | sed 's/^/    /' >&2
    [ "$ALLOW_DIRTY" = 1 ] || die "/opt/nxeon has uncommitted changes to tracked files (above). Commit them first — only the committed HEAD is built. (--allow-dirty to build HEAD anyway.)"
    warn "building committed HEAD; the uncommitted changes above are NOT included"
  fi
}

# Schema first (as before): additive changes are safe for the still-running old
# code, and the new build may prerender against them. Uses the BUILD tree's
# schema (= the commit being deployed) and production's DATABASE_URL, passed
# explicitly into a scrubbed environment.
hook_schema() {
  local dburl; dburl=$(db_url_of_env_file "$APP_DIR/.env")
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
    log "Schema (dry run): SQL a db push would apply to '$EXPECT_DB':"
    (cd "$BUILD_DIR" && clean_env DATABASE_URL="$dburl" npx prisma migrate diff \
       --from-url "$dburl" --to-schema-datamodel "$BUILD_DIR/prisma/schema.prisma" --script 2>&1 | tail -40 | sed 's/^/    /') || warn "could not compute the schema diff"
    return 0
  fi
  local flags=(--skip-generate --schema="$BUILD_DIR/prisma/schema.prisma") mode="additive only"
  if [ "$ACCEPT_DATA_LOSS" = 1 ]; then flags+=(--accept-data-loss); mode="--accept-data-loss"; fi
  log "Applying database schema to '$EXPECT_DB' ($mode)"
  local out rc=0
  out=$(cd "$BUILD_DIR" && clean_env DATABASE_URL="$dburl" npx prisma db push "${flags[@]}" 2>&1) || rc=$?
  echo "$out" | tail -6 | sed 's/^/    /'
  [ "$rc" = 0 ] || die "prisma db push failed/refused (exit $rc). Nothing else changed; the live app is untouched. If the warning above is a reviewed, accepted data-loss change, re-run with --accept-data-loss."
}

# The worker runs `npx tsx worker/index.ts` from /opt/nxeon's own source and
# node_modules, so it needs deps + a Prisma client generated THERE — done only
# after the web is confirmed healthy, so it can never delay the web cutover.
hook_after_web() {
  if [ "$(git -C "$APP_DIR" rev-parse HEAD)" != "$TARGET_COMMIT" ]; then
    warn "/opt/nxeon HEAD moved during the deploy ($(git -C "$APP_DIR" rev-parse --short HEAD) != ${TARGET_COMMIT:0:10}); the worker will run the NEWER source. Run promote again."
  fi
  install_and_generate "$APP_DIR"
  # .env stays nxeon-owned + 0600: Prisma opens it directly as the web user.
  chown "$WEB_USER:$WEB_USER" "$APP_DIR/.env" 2>/dev/null || true
  chmod 600 "$APP_DIR/.env" 2>/dev/null || true
  check_units "$APP_DIR"
  wait_for_provisions
  log "Restarting $WORKER_SERVICE"
  systemctl restart "$WORKER_SERVICE"
  sleep 5
  systemctl is-active "$WEB_SERVICE" "$WORKER_SERVICE" || warn "$WORKER_SERVICE is not active — check journalctl -u $WORKER_SERVICE (the web is already live and healthy)"
}

TARGET_COMMIT=$(git -C "$REPO_DIR" rev-parse HEAD)
run_release_pipeline "$TARGET_COMMIT"
#!/bin/bash
# Instant web rollback (or roll-forward) to a kept release — no build.
#
#   scripts/rollback-release.sh --production|--staging            # previous release
#   scripts/rollback-release.sh --production|--staging RELEASE_ID # a specific one
#   scripts/rollback-release.sh --production|--staging --list
#
# Swaps the live .next symlink to that release in one atomic rename, restarts
# the web service and health-checks it (/, a real static chunk, the release's
# _buildManifest.js, /login). If that release is unhealthy it swaps straight
# back. Takes the same per-environment lock as a deploy.
#
# NOT rolled back: the worker (it runs from the live tree's git source — check
# out the old commit there and restart the worker if you need that too) and the
# database schema (pushes are additive, so the old code keeps working).
# --force is needed to deploy a release staged by --dry-run (its schema was
# never pushed).
set -euo pipefail
ENV_NAME=""; WANT=""; LIST=0; FORCE=0; TEST_CONFIG=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  a="$1"; shift
  case "$a" in
    --test-config) TEST_CONFIG="$1"; ENV_NAME=test; shift ;;   # test harness only
    --production) ENV_NAME=production ;;
    --staging) ENV_NAME=staging ;;
    --list) LIST=1 ;;
    --force) FORCE=1 ;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,18p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    -*) echo "unknown option: $a" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    *) WANT="$a" ;;
  esac
done
case "$ENV_NAME" in
  production|staging) source "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/lib/seamless-env-$ENV_NAME.sh" ;;
  test) # shellcheck disable=SC1090
        source "$TEST_CONFIG" ;;   # throwaway test app (sets APP_DIR, WEB_SERVICE, ...)
  *) echo "say --production or --staging" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
RELEASES_DIR="$DEPLOY_ROOT/releases"
source "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/lib/seamless-release.sh"
[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || die "run as root"
RELEASES_DIR=$(realpath "$RELEASES_DIR")

CUR=$(release_id_of_target "$(current_target)")
if [ "$LIST" = 1 ]; then
  echo "Live: $CUR"
  for r in $(list_releases); do
    mark=" "; [ "$r" = "$CUR" ] && mark="*"
    note=""; [ -f "$RELEASES_DIR/$r/DEPLOYED" ] && note="  deployed $(cat "$RELEASES_DIR/$r/DEPLOYED")"
    grep -q '"dryRun":true' "$RELEASES_DIR/$r/release.json" 2>/dev/null && note="$note  (dry-run, schema never pushed)"
    echo " $mark $r$note"
  done
  exit 0
fi

acquire_env_lock "$ENV_NAME"
trap 'rm -f "$APP_DIR/.next.incoming" "$APP_DIR/.next.rollback" 2>/dev/null; seamless_cleanup' EXIT
trap 'warn "interrupted"; exit 130' INT TERM HUP

if [ -z "$WANT" ]; then
  [ "$CUR" = legacy ] && die "the live build predates release dirs — nothing older to roll back to (a .next.legacy-* dir, if present, can be restored by hand with mv -T --exchange)."
  # newest release older than the live one that was actually deployed + healthy once
  for r in $(list_releases); do
    [ "$r" = "$CUR" ] && break
    [ -f "$RELEASES_DIR/$r/DEPLOYED" ] && WANT="$r"
  done
  [ -n "$WANT" ] || die "no previously-deployed release older than the live one ($CUR) — see --list"
fi
[ -f "$RELEASES_DIR/$WANT/.next/standalone/server.js" ] || die "no such release: $WANT (see --list)"
[ "$WANT" = "$CUR" ] && die "$WANT is already live"
if grep -q '"dryRun":true' "$RELEASES_DIR/$WANT/release.json" 2>/dev/null && [ "$FORCE" != 1 ]; then
  die "$WANT was staged by --dry-run; its schema was never pushed. Re-run with --force if you are sure."
fi

log "Switching $ENV_NAME web: $CUR -> $WANT"
if cutover_to "$RELEASES_DIR/$WANT/.next"; then
  log "Done. Live: $WANT. (Worker and DB schema unchanged.)"
else
  die "Release $WANT was unhealthy — swapped back to $CUR."
fi
seamless-env-production.sh
seamless-env-staging.sh
seamless-release.sh

12	    12	# prod half-dead for 11 minutes, and two concurrent promotes collided
13	    13	# (ENOTEMPTY .next/export).
14	    14	#
15	    15	# THE MODEL:
16	    16	#   build dir   $DEPLOY_ROOT/build                 git worktree of the target
17	    17	#               (on the ZFS pool, /tank — the     commit + its OWN node_modules +
18	    18	#               root disk is ~90% full)            a copy of the live .env
19	    19	#   releases    $DEPLOY_ROOT/releases/<UTC>-<sha>-<BUILD_ID>/.next
20	    20	#               finished .next (standalone + static + public + geoip data),
21	    21	#               chowned for the web user; last $KEEP_RELEASES kept
22	    22	#   live        $APP_DIR/.next  ->  SYMLINK to the current release's .next
23	    23	#
24	    24	# Cutover = one atomic rename of that symlink + `systemctl restart`. No unit
25	    25	# file changes are needed: the unit still runs `node .next/standalone/server.js`
26	    26	# from $APP_DIR; node resolves the symlink, so the running process's own files
27	    27	# (an older release dir) are never modified underneath it. The first cutover
28	    28	# converts the legacy real .next directory into the symlink with a single
29	    29	# renameat2(RENAME_EXCHANGE) (`mv --exchange`), so .next never stops existing.
30	    30	#
31	    31	# Nothing in here ever writes INTO $APP_DIR/.next.
32	    32	# =============================================================================

34	    34	# ---- defaults (wrappers set the environment-specific ones before sourcing) --
35	    35	: "${KEEP_RELEASES:=3}"            # releases kept besides the current one
36	    36	: "${BUILD_MAX_MIN:=20}"           # hard cap on total build time
37	    37	: "${BUILD_STALL_MIN:=5}"          # kill if no progress for this long
38	    38	: "${BUILD_STALL_CPU_SEC:=20}"     # "progress" = >= this much CPU burned since last mark, or log growth
39	    39	: "${BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_SEC:=1800}"   # wait this long for another env's build to finish
40	    40	: "${MIN_MEM_AVAIL_MB:=4096}"      # refuse to build below this MemAvailable
41	    41	: "${MIN_BUILD_DISK_GB:=8}"        # free space needed where the build/releases live
42	    42	: "${MIN_APP_DISK_MB:=300}"        # free space needed on the live tree's filesystem
43	    43	: "${HEALTH_TIMEOUT_SEC:=90}"      # how long a restarted web gets to answer 200
44	    44	: "${HEALTH_EXTRA_PATHS:=/login}"  # extra paths that must answer 200 (space-separated)
45	    45	: "${PRESMOKE:=1}"                 # boot the new release on a side port before cutover

78	    78	# ---- locking ----------------------------------------------------------------
79	    79	# One deploy per environment at a time (fails fast), and one `next build` on
80	    80	# the whole box at a time (waits) — a staging and a production build running
81	    81	# together is exactly what pushed swap to 100% on 2026-10-01.
82	    82	acquire_env_lock() {
83	    83	  local name="$1"
84	    84	  exec 8>>"/run/lock/nxeon-deploy-${name}.lock"
85	    85	  if ! flock -n 8; then
86	    86	    die "another ${name} deploy/rollback is already running (lock /run/lock/nxeon-deploy-${name}.lock). Refusing to start a second one."
87	    87	  fi

92	    92	  flock -w "$BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_SEC" 7 || die "timed out waiting for /run/lock/nxeon-build.lock (another build is running)"
93	    93	  "$@"
94	    94	  local rc=$?
95	    95	  flock -u 7
96	    96	  return $rc
97	    97	}

141	   141	prepare_build_tree() {
142	   142	  local commit="$1"
143	   143	  if [ ! -e "$BUILD_DIR/.git" ]; then
144	   144	    log "Creating build worktree $BUILD_DIR (detached at ${commit:0:10})"
145	   145	    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$BUILD_DIR")"
146	   146	    git -C "$REPO_DIR" worktree prune
147	   147	    git -C "$REPO_DIR" worktree add --detach "$BUILD_DIR" "$commit" >/dev/null
148	   148	  else
149	   149	    log "Checking out ${commit:0:10} in $BUILD_DIR"
150	   150	    git -C "$BUILD_DIR" checkout -q -f --detach "$commit"
151	   151	    # Untracked-but-not-ignored leftovers only; node_modules/.next/.env are ignored and kept.
152	   152	    git -C "$BUILD_DIR" clean -q -fd
153	   153	  fi
154	   154	  [ "$(git -C "$BUILD_DIR" rev-parse HEAD)" = "$commit" ] || die "build tree is not at $commit"
155	   155	  # node_modules in the build tree must be its own (never a symlink into a live tree).
156	   156	  local d
157	   157	  for d in node_modules node_modules/.prisma node_modules/@prisma; do
158	   158	    [ -L "$BUILD_DIR/$d" ] && die "$BUILD_DIR/$d is a symlink — the build tree must own its node_modules"
159	   159	  done

161	   161	  # and every build-time value match where this release will run. The other
162	   162	  # .env.* files Next.js reads are mirrored too (copied if the live tree has
163	   163	  # them, removed if it does not) so the build sees exactly what an in-place
164	   164	  # build would have.
165	   165	  install -m 600 -o root -g root "$APP_DIR/.env" "$BUILD_DIR/.env"
166	   166	  local extra
167	   167	  for extra in .env.local .env.production .env.production.local; do
168	   168	    if [ -f "$APP_DIR/$extra" ]; then install -m 600 "$APP_DIR/$extra" "$BUILD_DIR/$extra"; else rm -f "$BUILD_DIR/$extra"; fi
169	   169	  done
170	   170	  cmp -s "$APP_DIR/.env" "$BUILD_DIR/.env" || die "build .env copy differs from $APP_DIR/.env"

174	   174	    find "$BUILD_DIR/.next" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -name cache -exec rm -rf {} +
175	   175	  fi

206	   206	# ---- build with watchdog ----------------------------------------------------
207	   207	# The build runs in its own SESSION (setsid). Track and kill by session id, not
208	   208	# process group: tools like `timeout` move their child into a new process
209	   209	# group, but nothing in a build calls setsid, so the session holds the whole tree.
210	   210	session_pids() {
211	   211	  awk -v sid="$1" '{ line=$0; sub(/^.*\) /, "", line); split(line, f, " ");
212	   212	      # after "comm) ": f[1]=state f[2]=ppid f[3]=pgrp f[4]=session
213	   213	      if (f[4]==sid) { split(FILENAME, p, "/"); print p[3] } }' /proc/[0-9]*/stat 2>/dev/null
214	   214	}
215	   215	# Sum of utime+stime+cutime+cstime (clock ticks) of every process in a session.
216	   216	session_cpu_ticks() {
217	   217	  awk -v sid="$1" '{ line=$0; sub(/^.*\) /, "", line); split(line, f, " ");
218	   218	      if (f[4]==sid) t+=f[12]+f[13]+f[14]+f[15] }
219	   219	    END { print t+0 }' /proc/[0-9]*/stat 2>/dev/null
220	   220	}
221	   221	kill_session() {
222	   222	  local sid="$1" i pids
223	   223	  pids=$(session_pids "$sid"); [ -n "$pids" ] && kill -TERM $pids 2>/dev/null || true
224	   224	  for i in $(seq 1 15); do
225	   225	    [ -z "$(session_pids "$sid")" ] && return 0
226	   226	    sleep 1
227	   227	  done
228	   228	  pids=$(session_pids "$sid"); [ -n "$pids" ] && kill -KILL $pids 2>/dev/null || true
229	   229	}

231	   231	# run_watched LOGFILE CMD... — runs CMD in its own session under nice/ionice,
232	   232	# kills the whole session on stall or overall timeout. Returns CMD's exit code,
233	   233	# 124 on timeout, 125 on stall.
234	   234	run_watched() {
235	   235	  local logf="$1"; shift
236	   236	  local hz; hz=$(getconf CLK_TCK)
237	   237	  local poll="${WATCH_POLL_SEC:-15}"
238	   238	  : >"$logf"
239	   239	  local sidf; sidf=$(mktemp)
240	   240	  # --fork --wait: $pid is a waiter that exits with the build's status; the
241	   241	  # build itself is the leader of a brand-new session and writes its sid.
242	   242	  setsid --fork --wait bash -c 'echo $$ > "$0"; exec "$@"' "$sidf" \
243	   243	    nice -n 10 ionice -c2 -n7 "$@" >>"$logf" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
244	   244	  local pid=$! pg="" i
245	   245	  for i in $(seq 1 50); do pg=$(cat "$sidf" 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$pg" ] && break; sleep 0.1; done
246	   246	  rm -f "$sidf"
247	   247	  [ -n "$pg" ] || { kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null; die "watchdog: could not start the build in its own session"; }
248	   248	  WATCHED_SID="$pg"
249	   249	  local start=$SECONDS mark=$SECONDS cpu_mark size_mark cpu size
250	   250	  cpu_mark=$(session_cpu_ticks "$pg"); size_mark=$(stat -c %s "$logf")
251	   251	  local max=$((BUILD_MAX_MIN * 60)) stall=$((BUILD_STALL_MIN * 60)) need=$((BUILD_STALL_CPU_SEC * hz))
252	   252	  local verdict=""
253	   253	  while kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; do
254	   254	    sleep "$poll"
255	   255	    kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break
256	   256	    cpu=$(session_cpu_ticks "$pg"); size=$(stat -c %s "$logf")
257	   257	    if [ "$size" != "$size_mark" ] || [ $((cpu - cpu_mark)) -ge "$need" ]; then
258	   258	      mark=$SECONDS; cpu_mark=$cpu; size_mark=$size
259	   259	    fi
260	   260	    if [ $((SECONDS - start)) -ge "$max" ]; then verdict=timeout; break; fi
261	   261	    if [ $((SECONDS - mark)) -ge "$stall" ]; then verdict=stall; break; fi
262	   262	  done
263	   263	  if [ -n "$verdict" ]; then
264	   264	    warn "build ${verdict}: $( [ "$verdict" = timeout ] && echo "exceeded ${BUILD_MAX_MIN} min total" || echo "no output and < ${BUILD_STALL_CPU_SEC}s CPU for ${BUILD_STALL_MIN} min" ) — killing the build's whole session ($pg)"
265	   265	    kill_session "$pg"
266	   266	    wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
267	   267	    [ "$verdict" = timeout ] && return 124 || return 125
268	   268	  fi
269	   269	  local rc=0
270	   270	  wait "$pid" || rc=$?
271	   271	  WATCHED_SID=""
272	   272	  return $rc
273	   273	}

361	   361	# wait_healthy PORT BUILD_ID TIMEOUT [SIDE_UNIT] — "/" 200, a real /_next/static JS chunk
362	   362	# referenced by that HTML 200, this build's _buildManifest.js 200 (proves the
363	   363	# NEW build is the one answering), and every HEALTH_EXTRA_PATHS entry 200.
364	   364	wait_healthy() {
365	   365	  local port="$1" bid="$2" timeout="$3" unit="${4:-}" base="http://127.0.0.1:$1"
366	   366	  local tmp; tmp=$(mktemp)
367	   367	  local deadline=$((SECONDS + timeout)) code=""
368	   368	  while :; do
369	   369	    # A cold Next.js process answers its FIRST request only after ~10-20 s of
370	   370	    # module loading on this box, hence the generous per-request timeout.
371	   371	    code=$(curl -s -o "$tmp" -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 30 "$base/" || true)
372	   372	    [ "$code" = 200 ] && break
373	   373	    if [ -n "$unit" ] && ! systemctl is-active -q "$unit"; then
374	   374	      rm -f "$tmp"; HEALTH_FAIL="$unit exited before answering (last: ${code:-no answer})"; return 1
375	   375	    fi
376	   376	    if [ $SECONDS -ge $deadline ]; then rm -f "$tmp"; HEALTH_FAIL="GET / never returned 200 within ${timeout}s (last: ${code:-no answer})"; return 1; fi
377	   377	    sleep 1
378	   378	  done
379	   379	  local chunk; chunk=$(grep -oE '/_next/static/[^"'"'"' )]+\.js' "$tmp" | head -1)
380	   380	  rm -f "$tmp"
381	   381	  [ -n "$chunk" ] || { HEALTH_FAIL="GET / HTML references no /_next/static/*.js chunk"; return 1; }
382	   382	  code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 15 "$base$chunk" || true)
383	   383	  [ "$code" = 200 ] || { HEALTH_FAIL="static chunk $chunk returned ${code:-no answer}"; return 1; }
384	   384	  if [ -n "$bid" ]; then
385	   385	    code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 15 "$base/_next/static/$bid/_buildManifest.js" || true)
386	   386	    [ "$code" = 200 ] || { HEALTH_FAIL="/_next/static/$bid/_buildManifest.js returned ${code:-no answer} (is the new build really the one serving?)"; return 1; }
387	   387	  fi
388	   388	  local p
389	   389	  for p in $HEALTH_EXTRA_PATHS; do
390	   390	    code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 20 "$base$p" || true)
391	   391	    [ "$code" = 200 ] || { HEALTH_FAIL="GET $p returned ${code:-no answer}"; return 1; }
392	   392	  done
393	   393	  HEALTH_DETAIL="/ 200, $chunk 200${bid:+, _buildManifest($bid) 200}${HEALTH_EXTRA_PATHS:+, $HEALTH_EXTRA_PATHS 200}"
394	   394	  return 0
395	   395	}

397	   397	# start_side_instance UNIT PORT DOTNEXT — run DOTNEXT/standalone/server.js as
398	   398	# a transient systemd unit that mirrors the real one: same user, NODE_ENV, and
399	   399	# the live .env via EnvironmentFile= (minus PORT/HOSTNAME, which systemd would
400	   400	# otherwise let override ours). It binds all interfaces like the real unit (the
401	   401	# host firewall's input policy is drop for everything but 22/80/443/8080/8443).
402	   402	# Do NOT set HOSTNAME=127.0.0.1: Next then canonicalises to "localhost" and the
403	   403	# middleware answers GET / with a 301 (found while testing this).
404	   404	start_side_instance() {
405	   405	  local unit="$1" port="$2" target="$3" envf="$DEPLOY_ROOT/$1.env"
406	   406	  if ss -ltnH "sport = :$port" | grep -q .; then
407	   407	    die "port $port is already in use — cannot start $unit there"
408	   408	  fi
409	   409	  systemctl stop "$unit" 2>/dev/null || true
410	   410	  systemctl reset-failed "$unit" 2>/dev/null || true
411	   411	  ( umask 077; grep -vE '^(PORT|HOSTNAME)=' "$APP_DIR/.env" > "$envf" )
412	   412	  systemd-run --quiet --unit="$unit" -p User="$WEB_USER" -p Group="$WEB_USER" \
413	   413	    -p WorkingDirectory="$APP_DIR" -p EnvironmentFile="$envf" -p RuntimeMaxSec=900 \
414	   414	    -E NODE_ENV=production -E PORT="$port" \
415	   415	    /usr/bin/node "$target/standalone/server.js"
416	   416	}

422	   422	}

478	   478	# point_live_at TARGET_DOTNEXT — atomically make $APP_DIR/.next refer to TARGET.
479	   479	# Sets PREV_KIND (link|dir|none) and PREV_TARGET for undo.
480	   480	point_live_at() {
481	   481	  local target="$1" live="$APP_DIR/.next" tmp="$APP_DIR/.next.incoming"
482	   482	  [ -f "$target/standalone/server.js" ] || die "refusing to cut over: $target/standalone/server.js missing"
483	   483	  # NOTE: callers run this inside `if`, where set -e is off — every step is checked.
484	   484	  rm -f "$tmp"
485	   485	  ln -s "$target" "$tmp" || die "cannot create $tmp"
486	   486	  if [ -L "$live" ]; then
487	   487	    PREV_KIND=link; PREV_TARGET=$(readlink "$live")
488	   488	    mv -T "$tmp" "$live" || die "swap failed (live .next unchanged)"   # rename(2) over a symlink: atomic
489	   489	  elif [ -d "$live" ]; then
490	   490	    PREV_KIND=dir; PREV_TARGET="$APP_DIR/.next.legacy-$(now_utc)"
491	   491	    mv -T --exchange "$tmp" "$live" || die "swap failed (live .next unchanged)"  # renameat2(RENAME_EXCHANGE): atomic, .next never vanishes
492	   492	    mv -T "$tmp" "$PREV_TARGET" || die "swapped, but could not rename the old build ($tmp) to $PREV_TARGET"  # $tmp now holds the old real dir
493	   493	  elif [ ! -e "$live" ]; then
494	   494	    PREV_KIND=none; PREV_TARGET=""
495	   495	    mv -T "$tmp" "$live" || die "swap failed"
496	   496	  else
497	   497	    die "$live is neither a symlink nor a directory"
498	   498	  fi
499	   499	  log "Live .next -> $target (previous: ${PREV_KIND} ${PREV_TARGET})"
500	   500	}

505	   505	    link)
506	   506	      rm -f "$tmp"; ln -s "$PREV_TARGET" "$tmp" && mv -T "$tmp" "$live" || return 1 ;;
507	   507	    dir)
508	   508	      mv -T --exchange "$PREV_TARGET" "$live" || return 1  # real dir back to .next; symlink now at PREV_TARGET
509	   509	      [ -L "$PREV_TARGET" ] && rm -f "$PREV_TARGET" ;;
510	   510	    *) warn "no previous .next to roll back to" ; return 1 ;;
511	   511	  esac
512	   512	  log "Rolled live .next back to the previous build"
513	   513	}

537	   537	# new release while the real service restarts and warms (zero downtime);
538	   538	# otherwise the downtime is the restart + the cold first request.
539	   539	cutover_to() {

541	   541	  bid=$(build_id_of "$target")

546	   546	    fi

549	   549	    if ! wait_healthy "$GREEN_PORT" "$bid" "$HEALTH_TIMEOUT_SEC" "$gunit"; then

559	   559	      green=1
560	   560	    else
561	   561	      warn "could not move nginx to green — falling back to a plain restart cutover"
562	   562	      stop_side_instance "$gunit"
563	   563	    fi
564	   564	  fi
565	   565	  point_live_at "$target"

571	   571	    else
572	   572	      warn "COULD NOT POINT nginx BACK AT :$WEB_PORT — fix $NGINX_UPSTREAM_FILE by hand NOW (green on :$GREEN_PORT is serving, RuntimeMaxSec 15 min)"

578	   578	    return 0
579	   579	  fi
580	   580	  warn "NEW BUILD UNHEALTHY: $HEALTH_FAIL"
581	   581	  journalctl -u "$WEB_SERVICE" -n 20 --no-pager 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/    /' >&2 || true
582	   582	  warn "AUTO-ROLLBACK to the previous build$([ "$green" = 1 ] && echo " (traffic stays on green while the real service rolls back)")"

589	   589	    fi

591	   591	      warn "Rolled back; previous build is serving again ($HEALTH_DETAIL)."
592	   592	    else
593	   593	      warn "Rolled back, but $HEALTH_FAIL — check nginx + journalctl -u $WEB_SERVICE NOW."

603	   603	  return 1
604	   604	}

654	   654	# Compare deploy/*.service|*.timer against what systemd has installed. Units
655	   655	# are never copied silently: with INSTALL_UNITS=1 they are installed +
656	   656	# daemon-reloaded, otherwise the exact commands are printed.
657	   657	check_units() {
658	   658	  local src="$1" f name dst changed=()
659	   659	  for f in "$src"/deploy/*.service "$src"/deploy/*.timer; do
660	   660	    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
661	   661	    name=$(basename "$f"); dst="/etc/systemd/system/$name"
662	   662	    [ -f "$dst" ] || continue                    # only units that are actually installed here
663	   663	    cmp -s "$f" "$dst" || changed+=("$name")
664	   664	  done
665	   665	  [ ${#changed[@]} -eq 0 ] && { log "systemd units in deploy/ match the installed ones"; return 0; }
666	   666	  if [ "${INSTALL_UNITS:-0}" = 1 ]; then
667	   667	    for name in "${changed[@]}"; do
668	   668	      log "Installing changed unit $name"
669	   669	      install -m 644 "$src/deploy/$name" "/etc/systemd/system/$name" || { warn "could not write /etc/systemd/system/$name"; INSTALL_UNITS=0; }
670	   670	    done
671	   671	    [ "${INSTALL_UNITS}" = 1 ] && systemctl daemon-reload && return 0
672	   672	  fi
673	   673	  warn "deploy/ has changed unit(s) not installed: ${changed[*]}"
674	   674	  warn "Review with:  for u in ${changed[*]}; do diff -u /etc/systemd/system/\$u $src/deploy/\$u; done"
675	   675	  warn "Install with: for u in ${changed[*]}; do install -m 644 $src/deploy/\$u /etc/systemd/system/\$u; done && systemctl daemon-reload"
676	   676	  warn "(or re-run with --install-units). Restart the affected service afterwards."

content.thinking:
Primary has 8 threads but is contended with staging, so building on node-2 with 6 threads could be faster. Node-2 also runs its own staging copy and has Postgres 17 on localhost, which already holds sandbox/staging/v2 databases, so I should set up a dedicated role for throwaway agent DBs there carefully to avoid conflicts.

Rather than a role, running a fully separate Postgres cluster on port 5433 for agents is cleaner — isolated from the sandbox/staging/v2 data, no superuser access, and can be capped under the build slice via a systemd drop-in. I'll keep shared_buffers small and decide whether the data directory lives on rpool or tank, leaning toward the default location since rpool has plenty of free space.

For Node, I need to match the primary's exact version (v22.23.1) on node-2. Rather than downloading a fresh tarball and risking an npm version mismatch, copying the primary's actual node binary, bundled npm, and corepack directly into /opt/nxeon-build/node is safer and guarantees an identical setup — I should check how the primary's install is structured first.

The ARC on node-2 is capped at 0.38GB, which is fine for this purpose. Now I'm sketching the overall architecture: a systemd slice on node-2 with memory, CPU, IO, and task limits, a toolchain directory holding the exact Node version, a wrapper script that runs builds inside that scope with the right PATH, and a corresponding build directory on the tank.

For the git mirror itself, I need to figure out the sync direction—whether node-2 fetches from the primary over SSH or the primary pushes to node-2. Pushing from the primary seems safer since node-2 wouldn't need SSH access back to the primary, though since node-2 is itself a hypervisor with root access, the security distinction may not matter much; I still want to check what the owner intended by "fetch over SSH."

Also worth checking if /opt/nxeon has a GitHub origin remote, since node-2 could fetch directly from there instead. For path layout, I'm leaning toward mirroring the production build directory at an identical absolute path on node-2's tank to maximize reproducibility, though I should decide if the exact path really matters.

Checking /tank on node-2 shows only a "backup" directory, so I have a clean slate there. Rather than inventing a new path structure, I'll keep it symmetrical and simplest to reason about by using the same /tank/nxeon-deploy/production/build path on node-2, which makes the environment equivalence comparison cleaner.

For staging, the owner's instruction covers both dev work and production builds, but deploy-staging.sh currently builds on primary. I think the remote-build mechanism should be implemented generically in seamless-release.sh's library so it works for both production and staging environments, with staging's .env feeding into the build-env whitelist the same way. I'll default to enabling it for both since that reduces primary load, though I should still test to confirm it holds up for staging too.

But I realize the primary side still needs the prisma schema and CLI locally even if we skip the actual build step, since `prisma db push` runs against the build tree's node_modules -- so a lightweight npm install in the local checkout is still necessary even without running `next build`, since prisma generate isn't required for push with the skip-generate flag.

Since schema push skips generation anyway, prisma generate is cheap and keeping install_and_generate local keeps node_modules consistent, though it's unavoidable since the primary already needs npm install to supply the worker's prisma CLI for the schema push.

One option is to keep the local build worktree checkout git-only and let npm install run only when package-lock changes, skipping prisma generate locally — essentially reusing the existing prepare_build_tree flow as-is, which costs seconds normally and about a minute only when dependencies actually change. I consider having node-2 run prisma db push via an SSH tunnel to the primary's Postgres, but that would require production DB credentials on node-2, so I rule it out and start sketching the remote build flow: primary does preflight checks first.

For a remote build, memory thresholds can be relaxed since there's no local build happening, then the primary prepares its schema tree and pushes the target commit to node-2's mirror, ensuring node-2 has the commit. Next the primary generates a whitelisted build-env file from the live environment and securely copies it to node-2 with restricted permissions, keeping track of the commit hash, before running the schema hook and finally kicking off the actual remote build over SSH with a lock to prevent concurrent builds.

The remote build takes the lock, prepares the worktree from the mirror, writes the whitelisted env file, verifies no symlinks exist, installs dependencies, runs Prisma generate and the Next.js build inside a resource-controlled systemd scope with a watchdog timeout, then assembles the standalone output using the whitelisted env—afterward the primary swaps in the real .env with secure permissions during the finish-build step, since the build env on node-2 was only ever meant to be a placeholder.

To avoid version skew between node-2's installed scripts and the primary's current code, I'm deciding to have the primary concatenate its own seamless-release.sh and a buildhost-remote script and pipe them directly over SSH into bash on node-2, so node-2 only needs the underlying infrastructure (slice, toolchain, mirror) while the actual build logic always matches whatever the primary is currently running.

Scp'ing then invoking remote-build.sh directly avoids stdin problems entirely. For resource control, I'll run the build under systemd-run with --scope under the nxeon-build.slice, which puts the process in a transient scope governed by that slice's limits.

But an SSH drop issue needs solving: a scope tied to the SSH session dies on hangup, orphaning the build. Running it as a transient systemd service instead (--unit with --wait --pipe --collect) decouples the build from the SSH connection so it survives disconnects, with the primary just needing to handle reattachment or streaming through --pipe.

If SSH itself drops, the primary reports the failure but leaves the remote unit running; the EXIT trap then stops it via systemctl stop if still active, mirroring the kill_session behavior. I'm adding resource limits like nice priority, IO scheduling, and a runtime cap, while keeping run_watched inside for stall detection.

Then on the primary side, I'm rsyncing the built .next directory back from node-2 into the local build tree, overwriting it, and then running finish_build_tree locally to re-copy public/static/geoip assets, which is safe since the local tree is on the same commit.

The node-2-to-primary link is high latency since it's going to Singapore, so rsync's delta transfer becomes important — it should skip unchanged node_modules files via rolling checksums even though mtimes differ, and compression helps too. The main concern is that finish_build_tree on the primary still re-copies public/static into the same standalone paths that rsync already brought over.

I'm realizing the delta basis needs a persistent local directory, so rsyncing directly into BUILD_DIR/.next is risky since prepare_build_tree wipes that folder except cache — I need to skip that cleanup step in remote mode so the delta basis survives between runs, though that raises worries about partial rsync failures corrupting state.

To guard against that, I'll make rsync failures fatal and verify the local BUILD_ID matches what the remote reports after transfer, plus do a cheap sanity check comparing file counts since rsync's own checksums already handle integrity. I'm also weighing whether to rsync into a separate "incoming" staging directory instead and have stage_release move things over from there.

Since rsync -a preserves ownership and symlinks, stage_release will chown things properly afterward; I should also exclude the webpack cache, trace, and types directories from the node-2 transfer since they're large and unnecessary. The rest of the pipeline—finish_build_tree, stage_release, presmoke, cutover, hook_after_web, prune—stays unchanged, though I need to check whether standalone output has hard-coded absolute paths baked into server.js.

I'm also thinking through env handling: node-2's build .env is non-secret and gets replaced by finish_build_tree, while the primary's local .env stays real since prepare_build_tree copies it directly, so assert_env_targets_expected_db works correctly in both cases. The --build-local flag should just fall back to today's pipeline unchanged, but I'm now worried about the shared build lock on node-2 — if agents hold it during heavy builds, production promotion could stall, so I need some way to give production priority over agent builds for that lock.

Using flock with a wait timeout so agent builds yield, but still giving prod up to 30 minutes feels reasonable, similar to today's behavior. The bigger concern is memory contention: if prod and an agent's build run concurrently in the same cgroup slice with a shared memory cap, one could OOM-kill the other, so I'm considering splitting into parent/child slices — a prod sub-slice with memory protection and higher CPU weight, and a separate agents sub-slice with a lower cap and lower priority, so production builds get guaranteed resources under contention.

Setting agents to MemoryMax=6G leaves prod with only about 4G guaranteed out of the 10G parent, but a single build peak around 7G means that's not enough headroom for prod alone.

With 14G free and no swap on node-2, I shouldn't allocate more than roughly 10G total. I'm considering using the node-2 build lock so prod builds and agents' heavy jobs (full test suites, next build) stay mutually exclusive, while lighter agent work like tsc or a dev server stays capped at 6G without needing the lock. I should check whether the prod build sets NODE_OPTIONS max-old-space-size, since it currently doesn't, and measure the actual peak RSS via the cgroup's memory.peak for that unit.

I'm also noticing that the VM memory allocations on node-2 sum to about 64GB, which exceeds the physical 62GB -- meaning ballooning or KSM must be compensating. That 14G of "free" memory is shaky, since growing VMs could eat into it, and with no swap, a 10G build slice risks pushing the host into a global OOM rather than just reclaiming within its own MemoryMax cgroup.

To steer any global OOM away from killing a VM process, I want to raise the OOM score for build processes so the kernel targets them first. Since scope units don't support exec-level properties like OOMScoreAdjust, I plan to wrap commands with `choom -n 1000 --` to set the oom_score_adj directly, which children inherit, and I'll also add a preflight check on node-2 to block starting new builds if memory pressure looks too high.

For CPU, I want to cap build processes with CPUQuota and a lower CPUWeight so VMs win under contention. For agent workflows, since they run on the primary but need to act on node-2, I'm sketching out a `scripts/devhost` helper with subcommands to sync refs and create isolated worktrees with their own branch, dependency install, and Prisma generation.

Each worktree also gets a throwaway database and a scoped .env with dummy secrets, so I'm adding commands to run arbitrary commands inside that worktree's slice, trigger builds with locking, and spin up dev servers as transient units accessible via SSH tunnel. I'm rounding out the toolset with stop, remove, list, and fetch commands so agents can pull their committed work back into the primary repo from node-2.

But I'm realizing the sync direction is tricky: if the primary mirrors from node-2 with prune, it'll wipe out agent-only branches, so I need a push strategy that updates branches without deleting node-2-local ones -- maybe namespacing agent branches or pushing into a dedicated refs namespace instead of a straight mirror.

Also, I should check whether agents actually need their edit tools to run against the primary filesystem, since that changes the whole architecture.

Right — Claude Code's Read/Edit tools work on the primary's filesystem, so if worktrees are moved to node-2, agents lose direct access. A fix would be keeping source worktrees on the primary for editing, then syncing to node-2 (excluding node_modules/.next) only for heavy operations like builds, tests, and the dev server.

I'll go with syncing via a `devhost run` command: it operates on the current worktree, mirrors git-tracked plus untracked-not-ignored files to node-2's matching directory, then executes the command remotely — giving agents fast local edits and remote compute without needing fragile sshfs mounts.

For node_modules, node-2 installs natively (npm ci when the lockfile changes) rather than syncing it. Results can be pulled back with a `devhost pull` command, and while this setup doesn't strictly need the git mirror for dev work, keeping the mirror is worthwhile for prod builds since checking out an exact commit hash is more verifiable than rsyncing source. I'm also considering whether agent worktrees on the primary even need node_modules at all — probably not, avoiding the symlink hassle entirely.

For the throwaway database, I'm setting up a dedicated Postgres cluster on node-2's port 5433, where `devhost db create` makes a per-worktree database owned by a restricted `nxeon_agent` role with CREATEDB but no superuser or ownership-transfer privileges, since agents shouldn't run REASSIGN/DROP OWNED commands. Having the agent role create its own database (so it's automatically the owner) avoids any ownership-command issues, and since this cluster is fully throwaway and separate, it's harmless either way. I'm also sketching out the dev .env file devhost would write per worktree, including the database URL pointing to this throwaway DB, a random auth secret, and the app URL.

I want this environment to be minimal and safe, avoiding real infra credentials so agents running dev servers can't accidentally hit production systems. Rather than copying from the sandbox's real .env, I'll generate a bare-bones dev env with just the essentials, letting agents add extra vars locally if needed but never prod secrets. For syncing schema, `devhost db push` would run Prisma's push command with accept-data-loss against the throwaway DB, which is safe since it's isolated on the agents cluster.

I still need to check what db-target-guard.ts actually enforces, and figure out whether installing Playwright browsers and their apt dependencies on node-2, a Proxmox hypervisor, is acceptable given it's already done on the primary -- I should verify existing chromium libs there before deciding.

For dev server access, binding to 127.0.0.1 on node-2 and tunneling via ssh/devhost should be sufficient without opening firewall ports. I also want to confirm git remote configuration and whether the primary node's install setup matters here.

#!/bin/bash
# npm prebuild/predev guard. In a live tree (/opt/nxeon, /opt/nxeon-staging)
# .next is a SYMLINK to the release the running server is serving from
# (scripts/lib/seamless-release.sh). `next build` / `next dev` there would wipe
# or rewrite that live release in place — a worse version of the 2026-10-01
# outage. Build with scripts/promote-production.sh / deploy-staging.sh instead.
if [ -L .next ]; then
  echo "REFUSING: $(pwd)/.next is a symlink to a live release ($(readlink .next))." >&2
  echo "Do not build or run next dev in a live tree. Deploy with scripts/promote-production.sh or scripts/deploy-staging.sh." >&2
  exit 1

#!/bin/bash
# Three things (see 3. at the bottom) `next build` with output:"standalone" never does on its own —
# both confirmed live 2026-10-01 to take the whole site down when missed:
#
# 1. geoip-lite loads its .dat files off its own on-disk path at runtime
#    (not a statically-traceable require), so Next's standalone output
#    tracer misses them entirely — every request 500'd.
# 2. `.next/static` (every client JS/CSS chunk) is DOCUMENTED Next.js
#    behavior to NOT be copied into the standalone output — the site still
#    serves server-rendered HTML fine, but zero client JS loads, so nothing
#    hydrates: no interactivity, no animations, no working buttons anywhere.
#
# Both were fixed by hand mid-incident; this makes them permanent so no
# future build/deploy can reintroduce either outage.
set -euo pipefail

if [ -d "node_modules/geoip-lite/data" ] && [ -d ".next/standalone" ]; then
  mkdir -p ".next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite"
  cp -r "node_modules/geoip-lite/data" ".next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data"
  echo "[postbuild] copied geoip-lite data into standalone output"
fi

if [ -d ".next/static" ] && [ -d ".next/standalone/.next" ]; then
  rm -rf ".next/standalone/.next/static"
  cp -r ".next/static" ".next/standalone/.next/static"
  echo "[postbuild] copied .next/static into standalone output"
fi

# 3. `public/` (logo, favicon, flags, game art, brand assets) is ALSO not
#    copied into the standalone output (same documented Next.js behaviour).

content.content:
## Seamless deploys — release dirs, atomic cutover, rollback

**Why (2026-10-01).** `promote-production.sh` used to run `npm run build` inside `/opt/nxeon`.
`next build` deletes and rewrites `.next/` while `nxeon-web` (`node .next/standalone/server.js`,
`WorkingDirectory=/opt/nxeon`) is still serving from it: for 10-12 minutes per promote the HTML
rendered but every `/_next/static/*` chunk answered 400, lazy routes broke and `server.js` did not
exist. A hung build (11 min at ~1% CPU) left prod half-dead, and two concurrent promotes collided
(`ENOTEMPTY .next/export`). Staging had the same problem.

**The model** (code: `scripts/lib/seamless-release.sh`; per-env config:
`scripts/lib/seamless-env-{production,staging}.sh`):

```
 /tank/nxeon-deploy/<env>/build        git worktree of the target commit (ZFS pool — the root disk
                                        is ~90% full), its OWN node_modules + Prisma client, and a
                                        fresh byte-for-byte copy of the live .env (+ .env.local/
                                        .env.production* if the live tree has them)
 /tank/nxeon-deploy/<env>/releases/<UTC>-<sha8>-<BUILD_ID>/
     .next/                             finished build: standalone + static + public + geoip data,
                                        standalone/.env = live .env, chowned nxeon (no webpack cache)
     own-static.list  release.json  DEPLOYED (written once it served healthy)
 /opt/nxeon/.next  ->  SYMLINK to the live release's .next
```

No systemd unit change is needed: the unit still runs `node .next/standalone/server.js` from
`/opt/nxeon`; node resolves the symlink, so the running process's own files (an older release dir)
are never touched while it is still serving. The first run converts the old real `.next` directory
with one `renameat2(RENAME_EXCHANGE)` (`mv -T --exchange`) — `.next` never stops existing — and
keeps it as `/opt/nxeon/.next.legacy-<ts>` (webpack cache stripped at once, ~2.3 GB back on the root
disk; deleted after the next successful promote).

**Order of a promote** (`scripts/promote-production.sh`):

1. Refusals first: per-env `flock` (`/run/lock/nxeon-deploy-<env>.lock` — a second promote exits
   immediately), staging must be up + 200, `/opt/nxeon` must have no uncommitted changes to tracked
   files (only the committed HEAD is built; `--allow-dirty` overrides), `.env`'s `DATABASE_URL` must
   name database `nxeon` (staging: `nxeon_staging`), the deployed commit's `.gitignore` must list
   `/.next` + `/.next.*`,
   MemAvailable >= 4 GB (`MIN_MEM_AVAIL_MB`), >= 8 GB free on the pool, >= 300 MB on the root disk.
2. Build tree: checkout, `.env` copy (verified identical and pointing at the right DB), `npm install`,
   `prisma generate` — all in a scrubbed environment (`env -i`: a stray exported `DATABASE_URL` /
   `NODE_OPTIONS` in the operator's shell can no longer retarget anything). The generated client's
   baked `.env` path is asserted to resolve inside that tree.
3. Schema: `prisma db push --skip-generate` with the build tree's schema and production's URL,
   before the build (same ordering as before). **Additive only by default** — a change Prisma flags
   as possibly destructive aborts the promote before anything changed; re-run with
   `--accept-data-loss` after reviewing it (the old script always passed that flag). `--dry-run`
   prints the SQL a push would run (`prisma migrate diff`) instead.
4. Build: holds the box-wide `/run/lock/nxeon-build.lock` (a staging and a production build never
   run together), `nice 10` + `ionice -c2 -n7`, own session; the watchdog kills the whole session if
   there has been no log output and < 20 s CPU for 5 min (`BUILD_STALL_MIN`) or the build passes
   20 min total (`BUILD_MAX_MIN`). Then every old post-build step: `public/` + `.next/static` into
   standalone, geoip-lite data, `standalone/.env` = live `.env`.
5. Release dir staged; the previous release's own hashed static files are carried into it, so a tab
   opened before the deploy can still lazy-load its old chunks afterwards.
6. Pre-cutover smoke: the release boots as transient unit `seamless-presmoke-<env>` on :3095
   (staging :3096) with the same user + EnvironmentFile as the real unit; `/`, a real
   `/_next/static/*.js` chunk referenced by that HTML, `/_next/static/<BUILD_ID>/_buildManifest.js`
   (proves it is the NEW build answering) and `/login` must all be 200. Fails → nothing live changed.
7. Cutover: the `.next` symlink is replaced by one atomic rename, `systemctl restart nxeon-web`, the
   same health checks on :3000, then `http://127.0.0.1/` through nginx. Unhealthy → automatic
   rollback (symlink back, restart, re-check) and the promote exits 1 **without touching the worker**.
8. Worker (only after the web is healthy, so it can never delay the web): `npm install` + `prisma
   generate` in `/opt/nxeon` (scrubbed env, explicit `--schema`, baked `.env` path asserted =
   `/opt/nxeon/.env`), `.env` kept `nxeon:nxeon 0600`, `deploy/*.service|*.timer` compared with
   `/etc/systemd/system` (changed ones are printed with the exact diff/install commands, or installed +
   `daemon-reload`ed with `--install-units`), wait for RUNNING `PROVISION` jobs (max 4 min, as
   before), restart `nxeon-worker`.
9. Prune: keep the live release, the newest 3 releases that were deployed + healthy once, and the
   newest never-deployed one (a failed or dry-run build, for inspection).

**Downtime, measured** (throwaway copy of the staging build on its own port, transient systemd unit,
curl every 50 ms through a throwaway nginx during each cutover, box at load ~8.5 on 8 cores):

| Cutover mode | Connection refused | Hung requests | Errors seen by the probe |
|---|---|---|---|
| Old promote (build in place) | — | — | 10-12 min of 400s on every static chunk (2026-10-01 incident) |

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# Provision / refresh the Nxeon BUILD HOST on node-2 (nxeon-fsn1). Idempotent.
# Runs ON node-2 as root. Normally invoked from the primary by
#   scripts/buildhost/provision.sh
# which first ships the primary's exact Node toolchain to /opt/nxeon-build/node.
#
# WHY (2026-10-07): parallel agent builds on the primary (which serves the live
# site, Postgres and customer VMs) pushed load to 16+, filled swap and hard-
# crashed it once (2026-10-06). All `next build`s (production promotes and agent
# work) now run here, inside a capped systemd slice, on the tank SSD (customer
# VMs live on rpool/NVMe, so build IO never competes with their disks).
#
# What it sets up:
#   nxeon-build.slice            CPUQuota=600% (6 of 12 threads), MemoryMax=10G,
#                                no swap, low CPU/IO weight vs qemu.slice (VMs)
#     nxeon-build-prod.slice     production/staging release builds (priority)
#     nxeon-build-agents.slice   agent dev work (tsc, tests, dev servers, Playwright,
#                                throwaway Postgres) — capped lower
#   tank/nxeon-build             /tank/nxeon-build: mirror.git, wt/ (agent trees),
#                                npm-cache, pg-agents (throwaway DB cluster), logs
#   tank/nxeon-deploy            /tank/nxeon-deploy/<env>/build: release build trees
#   postgresql@17-agents         127.0.0.1:5433 ONLY, role nxeon_agent (CREATEDB,
#                                not superuser), for throwaway agent databases
#   /etc/nxeon-build/            root-only config (agents-db.env, <env>.build.env)
# Nothing here touches qemu.slice, customer VMs, or the existing 5432 cluster.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || { echo "run as root" >&2; exit 1; }
[ "$(hostname)" = nxeon-fsn1 ] || [ "${FORCE_HOST:-0}" = 1 ] || { echo "this is $(hostname), not node-2 (nxeon-fsn1); FORCE_HOST=1 to override" >&2; exit 1; }

TOOL=/opt/nxeon-build
BROOT=/tank/nxeon-build
DROOT=/tank/nxeon-deploy
log() { echo "==> $*"; }

[ -x "$TOOL/node/bin/node" ] || { echo "no toolchain at $TOOL/node — run scripts/buildhost/provision.sh from the primary" >&2; exit 1; }

# ---- ZFS datasets (tank = separate SATA SSD; VMs are on rpool) ----------------
mkds() {  # mkds NAME MOUNTPOINT QUOTA
  if ! zfs list -H "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    log "Creating dataset $1 at $2 (quota $3)"
    zfs create -o mountpoint="$2" -o compression=lz4 -o atime=off -o quota="$3" "$1"
  else
    zfs set quota="$3" "$1"
  fi
}
mkds tank/nxeon-build  "$BROOT" 300G
mkds tank/nxeon-deploy "$DROOT" 80G
mkdir -p "$BROOT"/{wt,npm-cache,logs,tmp,pw-browsers} "$DROOT"/{production,staging} /etc/nxeon-build
chmod 700 /etc/nxeon-build "$DROOT"
chmod 1777 "$BROOT/tmp"

# ---- slices ------------------------------------------------------------------
install_unit() {  # install_unit NAME <<content
  local f="/etc/systemd/system/$1" tmp; tmp=$(mktemp)
  cat > "$tmp"
  if ! cmp -s "$tmp" "$f" 2>/dev/null; then install -m 644 "$tmp" "$f"; log "Installed $f"; CHANGED=1; fi
  rm -f "$tmp"
}
CHANGED=0
install_unit nxeon-build.slice <<'EOF'
# Nxeon build host cap (scripts/buildhost/setup-node2.sh). Everything Nxeon
# builds or runs for development on node-2 lives under this slice. Customer VMs
# are in qemu.slice and are never limited by it.
[Unit]
Description=Nxeon builds + agent dev work (capped)
Before=slices.target

[Slice]
CPUAccounting=yes
MemoryAccounting=yes
IOAccounting=yes
TasksAccounting=yes
# 6 of 12 threads; low weight so VMs win any contention below the quota.
CPUQuota=600%
CPUWeight=20
# node-2 has no swap and ~14 GB free beside the VMs: hard 10 GB ceiling.
MemoryHigh=9500M
MemoryMax=10G
MemorySwapMax=0
IOWeight=10
TasksMax=8192
EOF
install_unit nxeon-build-prod.slice <<'EOF'
# Release builds for promote-production.sh / deploy-staging.sh (priority inside
# nxeon-build.slice: 10x the CPU weight of agent work, memory protected).
[Unit]
Description=Nxeon release builds (production/staging)
Before=slices.target

[Slice]
CPUWeight=1000
IOWeight=100
MemoryLow=6G
EOF
install_unit nxeon-build-agents.slice <<'EOF'
# Agent dev work (scripts/devhost): tsc, tests, dev servers, Playwright, agent
# next builds, and the throwaway Postgres cluster on 127.0.0.1:5433.
[Unit]
Description=Nxeon agent dev work (capped)
Before=slices.target

[Slice]
CPUWeight=100
IOWeight=20
MemoryHigh=5500M
MemoryMax=6G
EOF
[ "$CHANGED" = 1 ] && systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl start nxeon-build.slice nxeon-build-prod.slice nxeon-build-agents.slice

# ---- git mirror (pushed to FROM the primary; node-2 never needs SSH to it) ----
if [ ! -d "$BROOT/mirror.git" ]; then
  log "Creating bare mirror $BROOT/mirror.git"
  git init -q --bare "$BROOT/mirror.git"
fi
git -C "$BROOT/mirror.git" config core.logAllRefUpdates false
git -C "$BROOT/mirror.git" config gc.auto 256
git -C "$BROOT/mirror.git" config receive.denyNonFastForwards false
git -C "$BROOT/mirror.git" config uploadpack.allowAnySHA1InWant true

# ---- throwaway Postgres cluster for agents (127.0.0.1:5433) -------------------
PGV=17
if ! pg_lsclusters -h | awk '{print $1"/"$2}' | grep -qx "$PGV/agents"; then
  log "Creating Postgres cluster $PGV/agents on 127.0.0.1:5433 (data on $BROOT/pg-agents)"
  mkdir -p "$BROOT/pg-agents"; chown postgres:postgres "$BROOT/pg-agents"; chmod 700 "$BROOT/pg-agents"
  pg_createcluster "$PGV" agents --port 5433 --datadir "$BROOT/pg-agents/data" --start-conf auto \
    -- --auth-local=peer --auth-host=scram-sha-256 >/dev/null
fi
CONF=/etc/postgresql/$PGV/agents/conf.d
mkdir -p "$CONF"
cat > "$CONF/nxeon-agents.conf" <<'EOF'
# Throwaway agent databases only (scripts/buildhost/setup-node2.sh). Never public.
listen_addresses = '127.0.0.1'
port = 5433
max_connections = 120
shared_buffers = 256MB
work_mem = 8MB
maintenance_work_mem = 128MB
effective_cache_size = 1GB
# throwaway data: speed over durability
fsync = off
synchronous_commit = off
full_page_writes = off
EOF
chown -R postgres:postgres "/etc/postgresql/$PGV/agents"
mkdir -p "/etc/systemd/system/postgresql@$PGV-agents.service.d"
cat > "/etc/systemd/system/postgresql@$PGV-agents.service.d/slice.conf" <<'EOF'
[Service]
Slice=nxeon-build-agents.slice
OOMScoreAdjust=900
EOF
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable -q "postgresql@$PGV-agents.service"
systemctl restart "postgresql@$PGV-agents.service"
for _ in $(seq 1 20); do pg_isready -q -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 && break; sleep 0.5; done
pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 >/dev/null || { echo "agents cluster did not come up" >&2; exit 1; }
ss -ltnH 'sport = :5433' | grep -qv '127.0.0.1:5433' && { echo "5433 is listening on something other than 127.0.0.1 — refusing" >&2; exit 1; }

if [ ! -s /etc/nxeon-build/agents-db.env ]; then
  pw=$(head -c 24 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' | head -c 32)
  ( umask 077; printf 'AGENT_PGHOST=127.0.0.1\nAGENT_PGPORT=5433\nAGENT_PGUSER=nxeon_agent\nAGENT_PGPASSWORD=%s\n' "$pw" > /etc/nxeon-build/agents-db.env )
fi
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. /etc/nxeon-build/agents-db.env
runuser -u postgres -- psql -q -p 5433 -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -v pw="$AGENT_PGPASSWORD" <<'SQL'
SELECT 'create role' WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'nxeon_agent') \gset nr_
\if :{?nr_?column?}
CREATE ROLE nxeon_agent LOGIN CREATEDB NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEROLE NOREPLICATION;
\endif
ALTER ROLE nxeon_agent PASSWORD :'pw';
SQL
chmod 600 /etc/nxeon-build/agents-db.env

# ---- build lock + helper on PATH-less location --------------------------------
: >> /run/lock/nxeon-build.lock
cat > /etc/tmpfiles.d/nxeon-build.conf <<'EOF'
f /run/lock/nxeon-build.lock 0644 root root -
EOF

log "Build host ready:"
systemctl show nxeon-build.slice -p CPUQuotaPerSecUSec -p MemoryMax -p MemoryHigh -p MemorySwapMax -p CPUWeight -p IOWeight | sed 's/^/    /'
echo "    node $("$TOOL/node/bin/node" -v), npm $(PATH="$TOOL/node/bin:$PATH" npm -v)"
echo "    agents Postgres: $(pg_lsclusters -h | awk '$2=="agents"{print $1"/"$2" port "$3" "$4}')"

#!/bin/bash
# Run a command on node-2 INSIDE the capped build slice. Runs ON node-2.
# Called by scripts/devhost and scripts/lib/buildhost.sh from the primary.
#
#   run-capped.sh agents|prod [options] -- CMD [ARGS...]
#     --dir DIR        working directory (default /)
#     --unit NAME      transient unit name (default nxeon-run-<pid>)
#     --bg             start as a background service (dev servers); prints the unit
#                      name and returns. Stop with: systemctl stop NAME
#     --max SEC        RuntimeMaxSec (default 7200 foreground, 14400 --bg)
#     --env FILE       extra KEY=VALUE environment file (root-only), e.g. a worktree's
#                      dev env. NEVER a production .env.
#     --lock           hold /run/lock/nxeon-build.lock (one heavy job on node-2 at a
#                      time — `next build`, full test suites, Playwright suites)
#
# Foreground commands run as a transient SERVICE with --pipe --wait so CPU/memory
# accounting is reported when they finish, and they never leave the slice.
# Every process gets nice 10, ionice best-effort 7 and oom_score_adj 1000, so if
# node-2 ever runs out of memory the kernel kills build/dev processes, never a
# customer VM (qemu processes keep their default score).
set -euo pipefail
SLICE_KIND="${1:-}"; shift || true
case "$SLICE_KIND" in
  agents) SLICE=nxeon-build-agents.slice ;;
  prod)   SLICE=nxeon-build-prod.slice ;;
  *) echo "usage: run-capped.sh agents|prod [--dir D] [--unit N] [--bg] [--max S] [--env F] [--lock] -- CMD..." >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
DIR=/; UNIT=""; BG=0; MAX=""; ENVF=""; LOCK=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dir) DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --unit) UNIT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --bg) BG=1; shift ;;
    --max) MAX="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --env) ENVF="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --lock) LOCK=1; shift ;;
    --) shift; break ;;
    *) echo "unknown option $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
[ $# -gt 0 ] || { echo "no command" >&2; exit 2; }
[ "$(hostname)" = nxeon-fsn1 ] || { echo "run-capped.sh must run on node-2 (nxeon-fsn1), not $(hostname)" >&2; exit 1; }
systemctl is-active -q "$SLICE" || systemctl start "$SLICE"
TOOL=/opt/nxeon-build
UNIT="${UNIT:-nxeon-run-$$}"
case "$UNIT" in *[!A-Za-z0-9_.@-]*) echo "bad unit name $UNIT" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
[ -n "$MAX" ] || { [ "$BG" = 1 ] && MAX=14400 || MAX=7200; }

props=(--slice="$SLICE" -p Nice=10 -p IOSchedulingClass=best-effort -p IOSchedulingPriority=7
       -p OOMScoreAdjust=1000 -p RuntimeMaxSec="$MAX" -p WorkingDirectory="$DIR"
       -p KillMode=control-group -p TimeoutStopSec=20
       -E HOME=/root -E PATH="$TOOL/node/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"
       -E LANG=C.UTF-8 -E NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 -E npm_config_cache=/tank/nxeon-build/npm-cache
       -E npm_config_update_notifier=false -E TMPDIR=/tank/nxeon-build/tmp
       -E PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/tank/nxeon-build/pw-browsers)
[ -n "$ENVF" ] && props+=(-p EnvironmentFile="$ENVF")

if [ "$LOCK" = 1 ]; then
  exec 7>>/run/lock/nxeon-build.lock
  if ! flock -n 7; then
    echo "==> waiting for node-2's build lock (/run/lock/nxeon-build.lock; a release build or another heavy job is running)…" >&2
    flock -w "${BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_SEC:-1800}" 7 || { echo "timed out waiting for the build lock" >&2; exit 75; }
  fi
fi

if [ "$BG" = 1 ]; then
  systemctl reset-failed "$UNIT" 2>/dev/null || true
  systemd-run --quiet --unit="$UNIT" --collect "${props[@]}" -- "$@"
  echo "$UNIT"
  exit 0
fi
# --pipe: stdin/stdout/stderr are ours; --wait: exit status + resource summary.
exec systemd-run --quiet --pipe --wait --collect --unit="$UNIT" "${props[@]}" -- "$@"

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# Build ONE release on node-2 for promote-production.sh / deploy-staging.sh.
# Runs ON node-2 (inside nxeon-build-prod.slice, started by run-capped.sh) —
# never by hand unless you are debugging a release build.
#
#   remote-build.sh ENV COMMIT
#
# Input  (pushed by the primary just before):
#   mirror.git  refs/nxeon-deploy/ENV = COMMIT     (git push from the primary)
#   /etc/nxeon-build/ENV.build.env  (0600)         the BUILD-TIME env only — no
#                                                  secrets, DATABASE_URL is a dead
#                                                  placeholder (see buildhost.sh)
# Output: /tank/nxeon-deploy/ENV/build/.next       finished build incl. standalone
#         + public + .next/static + geoip data, ready for the primary to rsync.
#         The primary then installs the REAL .env into standalone/, pushes the
#         schema, stages, smoke-tests and cuts over — exactly as before.
# Last stdout line on success:  REMOTE_BUILD_OK BUILD_ID=<id> COMMIT=<sha> SECONDS=<n>
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
ENV_NAME="${1:?env}"; COMMIT="${2:?commit}"
case "$ENV_NAME" in production|staging) ;; *) echo "bad env $ENV_NAME" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
case "$COMMIT" in *[!0-9a-f]*|"") echo "bad commit $COMMIT" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# devhost — run agent dev work on the BUILD HOST (node-2), not on the primary.
#
# Edit files on the primary as usual (your own git worktree — never /opt/nxeon),
# then run every heavy command through this helper. It mirrors your worktree's
# source to node-2 (/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>, own node_modules there), runs the
# command inside the capped nxeon-build-agents.slice with a THROWAWAY database
# (Postgres on node-2 127.0.0.1:5433), and streams the output back.
#
#   scripts/devhost run [--lock] [--max SEC] -- CMD...   push + run CMD in the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost tsc                                  = run -- npx tsc --noEmit
#   scripts/devhost test [FILES...]                      = run --lock -- npx tsx --test ...
#   scripts/devhost build                                = run --lock -- npx next build
#   scripts/devhost dev [--port P]                       start `next dev` on node-2 (background unit)
#   scripts/devhost bg NAME [--port P] -- CMD...         any background process (worker, preview server)
#   scripts/devhost stop [NAME|all]                      stop this worktree's background units
#   scripts/devhost logs [NAME] [-n N] [-f]              journal of a background unit (default: dev)
#   scripts/devhost tunnel PORT [LOCAL_PORT]             ssh -L so the primary can curl/Playwright it
#   scripts/devhost pull REMOTE_PATH [LOCAL_DEST]        copy results (screenshots, reports) back
#   scripts/devhost push                                 just sync files (run does this itself)
#   scripts/devhost install                              force npm install + prisma generate there
#   scripts/devhost db push|reset|info                   throwaway DB: schema push / recreate / name
#   scripts/devhost env set KEY=VALUE | unset KEY | list extra env for this worktree (never prod secrets)
#   scripts/devhost rm                                   stop units, drop the throwaway DB, delete the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost ls | status | sync                   workspaces / node-2 load / push refs to node-2's mirror
#
# Rules: /root/agent-notes/BUILD-HOST.md. The node-2 copy is a build/run sandbox,
# not a place to edit or commit — your primary-side worktree stays the source of truth.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
# shellcheck source=lib/buildhost-env.sh
source "$HERE/lib/buildhost-env.sh"
REPO="${DEVHOST_REPO:-/opt/nxeon}"

die() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
say() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; }
q() { printf '%q ' "$@"; }

# ---- workspace identity -----------------------------------------------------
worktree_root() {
  local top; top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || die "run this inside your own git worktree of the Nxeon repo"
  top=$(readlink -f "$top")
  case "$top" in
    /opt/nxeon|/opt/nxeon-staging|/tank/nxeon-deploy/*) die "$top is a live/deploy tree. Create your own worktree first:  git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main" ;;
  esac
  [ -L "$top/.next" ] && die "$top/.next is a symlink (a live tree) — refusing"
  [ -L "$top/node_modules" ] && say "warning: $top/node_modules is a symlink — never 'git add -A' here (see BUILD-HOST.md). devhost does not need local node_modules at all."
  echo "$top"
}
ws_name() {
  local top="$1" n
  n=$(basename "$top" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | tr -c 'a-z0-9-\n' '-' | sed -E 's/-+/-/g; s/^-//; s/-$//' | cut -c1-40)
  [ -n "$n" ] || n=wt
  echo "${DEVHOST_NAME:-$n}"
}
init_ws() {
  TOP=$(worktree_root); NAME=$(ws_name "$TOP")
  case "$NAME" in *[!a-z0-9-]*|"") die "bad workspace name '$NAME' (DEVHOST_NAME=...)";; esac
  WS="$BH_ROOT/wt/$NAME"
  ENVF="/etc/nxeon-build/wt/$NAME.env"
  DBNAME="wt_$(echo "$NAME" | tr '-' '_')"
  PORT=$(( 4100 + $(printf '%s' "$NAME" | cksum | cut -d' ' -f1) % 800 ))
}

# Create the node-2 side once: dir, owner marker, throwaway DB, env file.
ensure_remote() {
  bh_ssh "bash -s" <<EOF >&2
set -euo pipefail
[ "\$(hostname)" = "$BUILD_HOST_NAME" ] || { echo "not node-2" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p $(q "$WS") /etc/nxeon-build/wt; chmod 700 /etc/nxeon-build/wt
mk=$(q "$WS/.devhost-owner")
if [ -f "\$mk" ] && [ "\$(cat "\$mk")" != $(q "$TOP") ]; then
  echo "workspace $NAME belongs to \$(cat "\$mk") — set DEVHOST_NAME=<unique> for $TOP" >&2; exit 1
fi
printf '%s\n' $(q "$TOP") > "\$mk"
. /etc/nxeon-build/agents-db.env
if [ ! -s $(q "$ENVF") ]; then
  sec=\$(head -c 48 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' | head -c 48)
  ( umask 077; cat > $(q "$ENVF") <<EOT
# devhost env for $NAME (node-2 only, throwaway). NEVER production values.
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://\$AGENT_PGUSER:\$AGENT_PGPASSWORD@127.0.0.1:5433/$DBNAME?connection_limit=10
AUTH_SECRET=\$sec
APP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:$PORT
PORT=$PORT
COOKIE_SECURE=false
NXEON_DEVHOST=1
NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=3072
EOT
  )
fi
export PGPASSWORD="\$AGENT_PGPASSWORD"
if ! psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 -U "\$AGENT_PGUSER" -d postgres -tAc "SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname='$DBNAME'" | grep -q 1; then
  createdb -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 -U "\$AGENT_PGUSER" $DBNAME && echo "created throwaway database $DBNAME (node-2 127.0.0.1:5433)"
fi
EOF
}

push_files() {
  # Source only: git-tracked + untracked-not-ignored files. node_modules, .next,
  # .git and every .env* stay where they are (rsync never deletes excluded files).
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  rsync -a --delete --compress --compress-choice=zstd -e "ssh $BH_SSH_OPTS" \
    --exclude=/.git --exclude=/node_modules --exclude=/.next --exclude='/.next.*' \
    --exclude='/.env' --exclude='/.env.*' --include='.env.example' --exclude='.env*' \
    --exclude=/.devhost-owner --exclude=/.devhost-deps --exclude='/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo' \
    --filter=':- .gitignore' \
    "$TOP/" "$BUILD_HOST:$WS/"
}

# npm install + prisma generate when package-lock.json / schema changed (or forced).
deps() {
  local force="${1:-0}"
  local remote; remote=$(q "$BH_TOOL/bin/run-capped.sh" agents --dir "$WS" --env "$ENVF" --unit "nxeon-dev-$NAME-deps" --max 1800 --)
  bh_ssh "cd $(q "$WS") && h=\$(cat package-lock.json prisma/schema.prisma 2>/dev/null | sha256sum | cut -c1-16) && if [ $force = 1 ] || [ ! -d node_modules ] || [ \"\$(cat .devhost-deps 2>/dev/null)\" != \"\$h\" ]; then echo 'devhost: installing deps on node-2 (npm install + prisma generate)…' >&2; $remote bash -c 'npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -3 && npx prisma generate 2>&1 | tail -1' && echo \"\$h\" > .devhost-deps; fi" </dev/null >&2
}

prepare() { init_ws; ensure_remote; push_files; deps 0; }

REMOTE_UNIT=""
cleanup_remote_unit() {
  if [ -n "$REMOTE_UNIT" ]; then
    bh_ssh "systemctl stop $(q "$REMOTE_UNIT") 2>/dev/null; true" </dev/null || true
  fi
}

run_remote() {  # run_remote LOCK MAX CMD...
  local lock="$1" max="$2"; shift 2
  local args=(agents --dir "$WS" --env "$ENVF" --unit "nxeon-dev-$NAME-$$")
  [ "$lock" = 1 ] && args+=(--lock)
  [ -n "$max" ] && args+=(--max "$max")
  REMOTE_UNIT="nxeon-dev-$NAME-$$"
  trap cleanup_remote_unit EXIT
  trap 'exit 130' INT TERM HUP
  local rc=0
  bh_ssh "$(q "$BH_TOOL/bin/run-capped.sh" "${args[@]}" -- "$@")" </dev/null || rc=$?
  REMOTE_UNIT=""
  return $rc
}

cmd="${1:-help}"; shift || true
case "$cmd" in
  help|-h|--help) sed -n '2,33p' "$0" ;;

  sync)
    # All local branches + tags -> node-2 mirror refs/remotes/primary/* (pruned
    # within that namespace only). Release builds push their exact commit too.
    GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh $BH_SSH_OPTS" git -C "$REPO" push -q --force --prune "$BUILD_HOST:$BH_MIRROR" \
      '+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/primary/*' '+refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*'
    say "mirror synced ($(git -C "$REPO" for-each-ref refs/heads | wc -l) branches)" ;;

  push) init_ws; ensure_remote; push_files; say "pushed $TOP -> node-2:$WS" ;;
  install) init_ws; ensure_remote; push_files; deps 1 ;;

  run)
    lock=0; max=""
    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
      case "$1" in --lock) lock=1; shift ;; --max) max="$2"; shift 2 ;; --) shift; break ;; *) break ;; esac
    done
    [ $# -gt 0 ] || die "usage: devhost run [--lock] [--max SEC] -- CMD..."
    [ "$lock" = 1 ] && [ -z "$max" ] && max=1500   # keep the shared lock bounded (release builds wait max 30 min)
    prepare
    run_remote "$lock" "$max" "$@" ;;

  tsc)   prepare; run_remote 0 1800 npx tsc --noEmit "$@" ;;
