#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# devhost — run agent dev work on the BUILD HOST (node-2), not on the primary.
#
# Edit files on the primary as usual (your own git worktree — never /opt/nxeon),
# then run every heavy command through this helper. It mirrors your worktree's
# source to node-2 (/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>, own node_modules there), runs the
# command inside the capped nxeon-build-agents.slice with a THROWAWAY database
# (Postgres on node-2 127.0.0.1:5433), and streams the output back.
#
#   scripts/devhost run [--lock] [--max SEC] -- CMD...   push + run CMD in the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost tsc                                  = run -- npx tsc --noEmit
#   scripts/devhost test [FILES...]                      = run --lock -- npx tsx --test ...
#   scripts/devhost build                                = run --lock -- npx next build
#   scripts/devhost dev [--port P]                       start `next dev` on node-2 (background unit)
#   scripts/devhost bg NAME [--port P] -- CMD...         any background process (worker, preview server)
#   scripts/devhost stop [NAME|all]                      stop this worktree's background units
#   scripts/devhost logs [NAME] [-n N] [-f]              journal of a background unit (default: dev)
#   scripts/devhost tunnel PORT [LOCAL_PORT]             ssh -L so the primary can curl/Playwright it
#   scripts/devhost pull REMOTE_PATH [LOCAL_DEST]        copy results (screenshots, reports) back
#   scripts/devhost push                                 just sync files (run does this itself)
#   scripts/devhost install                              force npm install + prisma generate there
#   scripts/devhost db push|reset|info                   throwaway DB: schema push / recreate / name
#   scripts/devhost env set KEY=VALUE | unset KEY | list extra env for this worktree (never prod secrets)
#   scripts/devhost rm                                   stop units, drop the throwaway DB, delete the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost ls | status | sync                   workspaces / node-2 load / push refs to node-2's mirror
#
# Rules: /root/agent-notes/BUILD-HOST.md. The node-2 copy is a build/run sandbox,
# not a place to edit or commit — your primary-side worktree stays the source of truth.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
# shellcheck source=lib/buildhost-env.sh
source "$HERE/lib/buildhost-env.sh"
REPO="${DEVHOST_REPO:-/opt/nxeon}"

die() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
say() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; }
q() { printf '%q ' "$@"; }

# ---- workspace identity -----------------------------------------------------
worktree_root() {
  local top; top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || die "run this inside your own git worktree of the Nxeon repo"
  top=$(readlink -f "$top")
  case "$top" in
    /opt/nxeon|/opt/nxeon-staging|/tank/nxeon-deploy/*) die "$top is a live/deploy tree. Create your own worktree first:  git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main" ;;
  esac
  [ -L "$top/.next" ] && die "$top/.next is a symlink (a live tree) — refusing"
  [ -L "$top/node_modules" ] && say "warning: $top/node_modules is a symlink — never 'git add -A' here (see BUILD-HOST.md). devhost does not need local node_modules at all."
  echo "$top"
}
ws_name() {
  local top="$1" n
  n=$(basename "$top" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | tr -c 'a-z0-9-\n' '-' | sed -E 's/-+/-/g; s/^-//; s/-$//' | cut -c1-40)
  [ -n "$n" ] || n=wt
  echo "${DEVHOST_NAME:-$n}"
}
init_ws() {
  TOP=$(worktree_root); NAME=$(ws_name "$TOP")
  case "$NAME" in *[!a-z0-9-]*|"") die "bad workspace name '$NAME' (DEVHOST_NAME=...)";; esac
  WS="$BH_ROOT/wt/$NAME"
  ENVF="/etc/nxeon-build/wt/$NAME.env"
  DBNAME="wt_$(echo "$NAME" | tr '-' '_')"
  PORT=$(( 4100 + $(printf '%s' "$NAME" | cksum | cut -d' ' -f1) % 800 ))
}

# Create the node-2 side once: dir, owner marker, throwaway DB, env file.
ensure_remote() {
  bh_ssh "bash -s" <<EOF >&2
set -euo pipefail
[ "\$(hostname)" = "$BUILD_HOST_NAME" ] || { echo "not node-2" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p $(q "$WS") /etc/nxeon-build/wt; chmod 700 /etc/nxeon-build/wt
mk=$(q "$WS/.devhost-owner")
if [ -f "\$mk" ] && [ "\$(cat "\$mk")" != $(q "$TOP") ]; then
  echo "workspace $NAME belongs to \$(cat "\$mk") — set DEVHOST_NAME=<unique> for $TOP" >&2; exit 1
fi
printf '%s\n' $(q "$TOP") > "\$mk"
. /etc/nxeon-build/agents-db.env
if [ ! -s $(q "$ENVF") ]; then
  sec=\$(head -c 48 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' | head -c 48)
  ( umask 077; cat > $(q "$ENVF") <<EOT
# devhost env for $NAME (node-2 only, throwaway). NEVER production values.
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://\$AGENT_PGUSER:\$AGENT_PGPASSWORD@127.0.0.1:5433/$DBNAME?connection_limit=10
AUTH_SECRET=\$sec
APP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:$PORT
PORT=$PORT
COOKIE_SECURE=false
NXEON_DEVHOST=1
NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=3072
EOT
  )
fi
export PGPASSWORD="\$AGENT_PGPASSWORD"
if ! psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 -U "\$AGENT_PGUSER" -d postgres -tAc "SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname='$DBNAME'" | grep -q 1; then
  createdb -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 -U "\$AGENT_PGUSER" $DBNAME && echo "created throwaway database $DBNAME (node-2 127.0.0.1:5433)"
fi
EOF
}

push_files() {
  # Source only: git-tracked + untracked-not-ignored files. node_modules, .next,
  # .git and every .env* stay where they are (rsync never deletes excluded files).
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  rsync -a --delete --compress --compress-choice=zstd -e "ssh $BH_SSH_OPTS" \
    --exclude=/.git --exclude=/node_modules --exclude=/.next --exclude='/.next.*' \
    --exclude='/.env' --exclude='/.env.*' --include='.env.example' --exclude='.env*' \
    --exclude=/.devhost-owner --exclude=/.devhost-deps --exclude='/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo' \
    --filter=':- .gitignore' \
    "$TOP/" "$BUILD_HOST:$WS/"
}

deps() {
  local force="${1:-0}"
  local remote; remote=$(q "$BH_TOOL/bin/run-capped.sh" agents --dir "$WS" --env "$ENVF" --unit "nxeon-dev-$NAME-deps" --max 1800 --)
  bh_ssh "cd $(q "$WS") && h=\$(cat package-lock.json prisma/schema.prisma 2>/dev/null | sha256sum | cut -c1-16) && if [ $force = 1 ] || [ ! -d node_modules ] || [ \"\$(cat .devhost-deps 2>/dev/null)\" != \"\$h\" ]; then echo 'devhost: installing deps on node-2 (npm install + prisma generate)…' >&2; $remote bash -c 'npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -3 && npx prisma generate 2>&1 | tail -1' && echo \"\$h\" > .devhost-deps; fi" </dev/null >&2
}

REMOTE_UNIT=""
cleanup_remote_unit() {
  if [ -n "$REMOTE_UNIT" ]; then
    bh_ssh "systemctl stop $(q "$REMOTE_UNIT") 2>/dev/null; true" </dev/null || true
  fi
}

  local lock="$1" max="$2"; shift 2
  local args=(agents --dir "$WS" --env "$ENVF" --unit "nxeon-dev-$NAME-$$")
  [ "$lock" = 1 ] && args+=(--lock)
  [ -n "$max" ] && args+=(--max "$max")
  REMOTE_UNIT="nxeon-dev-$NAME-$$"
  trap cleanup_remote_unit EXIT

  REMOTE_UNIT=""

    say "mirror synced ($(git -C "$REPO" for-each-ref refs/heads | wc -l) branches)" ;;

    bh_ssh "journalctl --no-pager -o cat -u $(q "nxeon-dev-$NAME-$which") $(q "${@:--n100}")" ;;

    rport="${1:?usage: devhost tunnel PORT [LOCAL_PORT]}"; lport="${2:-$rport}"
    say "forwarding primary 127.0.0.1:$lport -> node-2 127.0.0.1:$rport (Ctrl-C to close)"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    exec ssh $BH_SSH_OPTS -N -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes -L "127.0.0.1:$lport:127.0.0.1:$rport" "$BUILD_HOST" ;;

             bh_ssh "f=$(q "$ENVF"); grep -v '^$k=' \"\$f\" > \"\$f.tmp\" || true; chmod 600 \"\$f.tmp\"; mv \"\$f.tmp\" \"\$f\"" </dev/null && say "unset $k" ;;
      *) die "usage: devhost env list|set KEY=VALUE|unset KEY" ;;
    esac ;;

  rm)
    init_ws
    bh_ssh "for u in \$(systemctl list-units --plain --no-legend 'nxeon-dev-$NAME-*' | awk '{print \$1}'); do systemctl stop \"\$u\"; done

input.content:
# =============================================================================
# Remote release builds on the build host (node-2). SOURCED by
# scripts/lib/seamless-release.sh users on the PRIMARY (promote-production.sh,
# deploy-staging.sh) when BUILD_MODE=remote (the default; --build-local opts out).
#
# What moves to node-2: npm install + prisma generate + `next build` + the
# standalone post-build copies, for the EXACT commit being deployed.
# What stays on the primary: the target checkout (for the schema + public/ +
# geoip data), `prisma db push`, the real .env, staging the release, the
# pre-cutover smoke on :3095, the symlink cutover, restarts and rollback.
#
# BUILD-TIME ENV (what node-2 gets): a generated file, NOT the production .env.
# Determined 2026-10-07 by building the same commit on node-2 with only these
# values and comparing the output with the primary's own build (see
# docs/DOCUMENTATION.md "Build host (node-2)"):
#   - .env has no NEXT_PUBLIC_* keys, so nothing is inlined into client JS;
#   - next.config.ts reads NXEON_SANDBOX (unset in prod/staging) and freezes
#     BUILD_TIME itself;
#   - the only prerendered routes are /robots.txt, /locations, /manifest.webmanifest,
#     /opengraph-image and /icon.png. They read APP_URL (+ AI_TRAINING_CRAWLERS,
#     unset). Everything else is force-dynamic and reads its env at RUNTIME from
#     the real .env / systemd EnvironmentFile on the primary;
#   - middleware env is read at runtime (only Next's own internals are baked).
# So node-2 receives BUILD_ENV_KEYS copied from the live .env (only those that are
# set) plus DATABASE_URL pointing at a closed port (Prisma's module-level init
# and the one generateStaticParams that queries the catalogue fail fast instead
# of reaching any database). No secret ever leaves the primary.
# =============================================================================
# shellcheck source=buildhost-env.sh
source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/buildhost-env.sh"
: "${BUILD_ENV_KEYS:=APP_URL AI_TRAINING_CRAWLERS NXEON_SANDBOX}"
: "${BUILD_ENV_DB_PLACEHOLDER:=postgresql://nxeon_build:unused@127.0.0.1:1/${EXPECT_DB:-nxeon}?connect_timeout=1}"
: "${BH_RSYNC_TIMEOUT_SEC:=900}"

# Write the build-time env to stdout (never printed by the deploy itself).
bh_build_env() {
  local src="$1" k line
  echo "# Generated by scripts/lib/buildhost.sh for a ${ENV_NAME} release build on the build host."
  echo "# Build-time values only — NOT the ${ENV_NAME} .env. Regenerated on every build."
  echo "DATABASE_URL=$BUILD_ENV_DB_PLACEHOLDER"
  for k in $BUILD_ENV_KEYS; do
    line=$(grep -E "^${k}=" "$src" | tail -1 || true)
    [ -n "$line" ] && echo "$line"
  done
  return 0
}

bh_assert_host() {
  local h
  h=$(bh_ssh hostname </dev/null 2>/dev/null) || die "cannot reach the build host $BUILD_HOST over SSH (use --build-local to build on this box instead)"
  [ "$h" = "$BUILD_HOST_NAME" ] || die "$BUILD_HOST answered as '$h', expected '$BUILD_HOST_NAME'"
  bh_ssh "[ -x $BH_TOOL/node/bin/node ] && [ -d $BH_MIRROR ] && systemctl is-active -q nxeon-build.slice || systemctl start nxeon-build.slice" </dev/null \
    || die "build host is not provisioned — run scripts/buildhost/provision.sh (or --build-local)"
  local want have
  want=$(node -v)
  have=$(bh_ssh "$BH_TOOL/node/bin/node -v" </dev/null)
  [ "$want" = "$have" ] || die "build host Node is $have but this box runs $want — run scripts/buildhost/provision.sh to re-sync the toolchain"
}

# Push the commit + the scripts + the build env to node-2.
bh_prepare_remote() {
  local commit="$1"
  log "Build host: $BUILD_HOST_NAME ($BUILD_HOST) — pushing ${commit:0:10} to its mirror"
  GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh $BH_SSH_OPTS" git -C "$REPO_DIR" push -q --force "$BUILD_HOST:$BH_MIRROR" "$commit:refs/nxeon-deploy/$ENV_NAME" \
    || die "git push to the build host mirror failed"
  local libdir; libdir="$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  scp -q $BH_SSH_OPTS "$libdir/seamless-release.sh" "$libdir/../buildhost/remote-build.sh" "$libdir/../buildhost/run-capped.sh" \
      "$BUILD_HOST:$BH_TOOL/bin/" </dev/null || die "could not copy the build scripts to the build host"
  bh_ssh "chmod 755 $BH_TOOL/bin/remote-build.sh $BH_TOOL/bin/run-capped.sh" </dev/null
  bh_build_env "$APP_DIR/.env" | bh_ssh "umask 077; mkdir -p /etc/nxeon-build && cat > /etc/nxeon-build/$ENV_NAME.build.env.tmp && chmod 600 /etc/nxeon-build/$ENV_NAME.build.env.tmp && mv /etc/nxeon-build/$ENV_NAME.build.env.tmp /etc/nxeon-build/$ENV_NAME.build.env" \
    || die "could not write the build env on the build host"
  log "Build env sent: $(bh_build_env "$APP_DIR/.env" | grep -E '^[A-Z_]+=' | cut -d= -f1 | tr '\n' ' ')(DATABASE_URL = closed-port placeholder; no secrets)"
}

BH_REMOTE_UNIT=""
bh_stop_remote() {
  [ -n "$BH_REMOTE_UNIT" ] || return 0
  bh_ssh "systemctl stop $BH_REMOTE_UNIT 2>/dev/null; true" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  BH_REMOTE_UNIT=""
}

bh_remote_build() {
  local commit="$1" out rc=0 t0=$SECONDS
  BH_REMOTE_UNIT="nxeon-release-build-$ENV_NAME"
  bh_ssh "systemctl is-active -q $BH_REMOTE_UNIT" </dev/null && die "a $ENV_NAME release build is already running on the build host ($BH_REMOTE_UNIT)"
  log "Building on $BUILD_HOST_NAME in nxeon-build-prod.slice (6-thread / 10 GB cap) — log there: $BH_DEPLOY_ROOT/$ENV_NAME/build.log"
  out=$(mktemp)
  # --max: the remote watchdog (BUILD_MAX_MIN) fires first; this is the backstop.
  bh_ssh "BUILD_MAX_MIN=$BUILD_MAX_MIN BUILD_STALL_MIN=$BUILD_STALL_MIN BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_SEC=$BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_SEC \
      $BH_TOOL/bin/run-capped.sh prod --unit $BH_REMOTE_UNIT --max $(( (BUILD_MAX_MIN + 40) * 60 )) \
      -- env BUILD_MAX_MIN=$BUILD_MAX_MIN BUILD_STALL_MIN=$BUILD_STALL_MIN BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_SEC=$BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_SEC \
      $BH_TOOL/bin/remote-build.sh $ENV_NAME $commit" </dev/null 2>&1 | tee "$out" | sed 's/^/    /' || true
  rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
  BH_REMOTE_UNIT=""
  REMOTE_BUILD_ID=$(grep -oE '^REMOTE_BUILD_OK BUILD_ID=[A-Za-z0-9_-]+' "$out" | tail -1 | sed 's/.*BUILD_ID=//')
  rm -f "$out"
  [ "$rc" = 0 ] && [ -n "$REMOTE_BUILD_ID" ] || die "REMOTE BUILD FAILED on $BUILD_HOST_NAME (exit $rc after $((SECONDS - t0))s) — nothing was changed here; the live app is untouched. Re-run, or --build-local to build on this box."
  log "Remote build finished in $((SECONDS - t0))s (BUILD_ID $REMOTE_BUILD_ID)"
}

# Pull the finished .next into the local build tree (delta against the previous
# build that is still there; webpack cache / trace / types stay on node-2).
bh_fetch_build() {
  local t0=$SECONDS
  log "Fetching the build from $BUILD_HOST_NAME into $BUILD_DIR/.next"
  mkdir -p "$BUILD_DIR/.next"
  rm -f "$BUILD_DIR/.next/BUILD_ID"   # a failed/partial fetch can never pass as a finished build
  local rc=0
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  timeout "$BH_RSYNC_TIMEOUT_SEC" rsync -a --delete --compress --compress-choice=zstd --timeout=120 \
    -e "ssh $BH_SSH_OPTS" --exclude=/cache --exclude=/trace --exclude=/types --exclude=/BUILD_ID \
    "$BUILD_HOST:$BH_DEPLOY_ROOT/$ENV_NAME/build/.next/" "$BUILD_DIR/.next/" </dev/null || rc=$?
  [ "$rc" = 0 ] || die "rsync of the build from $BUILD_HOST_NAME failed (exit $rc) — nothing was changed; the live app is untouched."
  # BUILD_ID last: its presence means the whole tree arrived.
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  rsync -a -e "ssh $BH_SSH_OPTS" "$BUILD_HOST:$BH_DEPLOY_ROOT/$ENV_NAME/build/.next/BUILD_ID" "$BUILD_DIR/.next/BUILD_ID" </dev/null \
    || die "could not fetch BUILD_ID"
  local got; got=$(cat "$BUILD_DIR/.next/BUILD_ID")
  [ "$got" = "$REMOTE_BUILD_ID" ] || die "fetched BUILD_ID '$got' != remote build '$REMOTE_BUILD_ID' (did another build overwrite it?)"
  # Remote and local file lists must match exactly (names + sizes).
  local lsum rsum

# =============================================================================
# Remote release builds on the build host (node-2). SOURCED by
# scripts/lib/seamless-release.sh users on the PRIMARY (promote-production.sh,
# deploy-staging.sh) when BUILD_MODE=remote (the default; --build-local opts out).
#
# What moves to node-2: npm install + prisma generate + `next build` + the
# standalone post-build copies, for the EXACT commit being deployed.
# What stays on the primary: the target checkout (for the schema + public/ +
# geoip data), `prisma db push`, the real .env, staging the release, the
# pre-cutover smoke on :3095, the symlink cutover, restarts and rollback.
#
# BUILD-TIME ENV (what node-2 gets): a generated file, NOT the production .env.
# Determined 2026-10-07 by building the same commit on node-2 with only these
# values and comparing the output with the primary's own build (see
# docs/DOCUMENTATION.md "Build host (node-2)"):
#   - .env has no NEXT_PUBLIC_* keys, so nothing is inlined into client JS;
#   - next.config.ts reads NXEON_SANDBOX (unset in prod/staging) and freezes
#     BUILD_TIME itself;
#   - the only prerendered routes are /robots.txt, /locations, /manifest.webmanifest,
#     /opengraph-image and /icon.png. They read APP_URL (+ AI_TRAINING_CRAWLERS,
#     unset). Everything else is force-dynamic and reads its env at RUNTIME from
#     the real .env / systemd EnvironmentFile on the primary;
#   - middleware env is read at runtime (only Next's own internals are baked).
# So node-2 receives BUILD_ENV_KEYS copied from the live .env (only those that are
# set) plus DATABASE_URL pointing at a closed port (Prisma's module-level init
# and the one generateStaticParams that queries the catalogue fail fast instead
# of reaching any database). No secret ever leaves the primary.
# =============================================================================
# shellcheck source=buildhost-env.sh
source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/buildhost-env.sh"
: "${BUILD_ENV_KEYS:=APP_URL AI_TRAINING_CRAWLERS NXEON_SANDBOX}"
: "${BUILD_ENV_DB_PLACEHOLDER:=postgresql://nxeon_build:unused@127.0.0.1:1/${EXPECT_DB:-nxeon}?connect_timeout=1}"
: "${BH_RSYNC_TIMEOUT_SEC:=900}"

# Write the build-time env to stdout (never printed by the deploy itself).
bh_build_env() {
  local src="$1" k line
  echo "# Generated by scripts/lib/buildhost.sh for a ${ENV_NAME} release build on the build host."
  echo "# Build-time values only — NOT the ${ENV_NAME} .env. Regenerated on every build."
  echo "DATABASE_URL=$BUILD_ENV_DB_PLACEHOLDER"
  for k in $BUILD_ENV_KEYS; do
    line=$(grep -E "^${k}=" "$src" | tail -1 || true)
    [ -n "$line" ] && echo "$line"
  done
  return 0
}

bh_assert_host() {
  local h
  h=$(bh_ssh hostname </dev/null 2>/dev/null) || die "cannot reach the build host $BUILD_HOST over SSH (use --build-local to build on this box instead)"
  [ "$h" = "$BUILD_HOST_NAME" ] || die "$BUILD_HOST answered as '$h', expected '$BUILD_HOST_NAME'"
  bh_ssh "[ -x $BH_TOOL/node/bin/node ] && [ -d $BH_MIRROR ] && systemctl is-active -q nxeon-build.slice || systemctl start nxeon-build.slice" </dev/null \
    || die "build host is not provisioned — run scripts/buildhost/provision.sh (or --build-local)"
  local want have
  want=$(node -v)
  have=$(bh_ssh "$BH_TOOL/node/bin/node -v" </dev/null)
  [ "$want" = "$have" ] || die "build host Node is $have but this box runs $want — run scripts/buildhost/provision.sh to re-sync the toolchain"
}

# Push the commit + the scripts + the build env to node-2.
bh_prepare_remote() {
  local commit="$1"
  log "Build host: $BUILD_HOST_NAME ($BUILD_HOST) — pushing ${commit:0:10} to its mirror"
  GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh $BH_SSH_OPTS" git -C "$REPO_DIR" push -q --force "$BUILD_HOST:$BH_MIRROR" "$commit:refs/nxeon-deploy/$ENV_NAME" \
    || die "git push to the build host mirror failed"
  local libdir; libdir="$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  scp -q $BH_SSH_OPTS "$libdir/seamless-release.sh" "$libdir/../buildhost/remote-build.sh" "$libdir/../buildhost/run-capped.sh" \
      "$BUILD_HOST:$BH_TOOL/bin/" </dev/null || die "could not copy the build scripts to the build host"
  bh_ssh "chmod 755 $BH_TOOL/bin/remote-build.sh $BH_TOOL/bin/run-capped.sh" </dev/null
  bh_build_env "$APP_DIR/.env" | bh_ssh "umask 077; mkdir -p /etc/nxeon-build && cat > /etc/nxeon-build/$ENV_NAME.build.env.tmp && chmod 600 /etc/nxeon-build/$ENV_NAME.build.env.tmp && mv /etc/nxeon-build/$ENV_NAME.build.env.tmp /etc/nxeon-build/$ENV_NAME.build.env" \
    || die "could not write the build env on the build host"
  log "Build env sent: $(bh_build_env "$APP_DIR/.env" | grep -E '^[A-Z_]+=' | cut -d= -f1 | tr '\n' ' ')(DATABASE_URL = closed-port placeholder; no secrets)"
}

BH_REMOTE_UNIT=""
bh_stop_remote() {
  [ -n "$BH_REMOTE_UNIT" ] || return 0
  bh_ssh "systemctl stop $BH_REMOTE_UNIT 2>/dev/null; true" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  BH_REMOTE_UNIT=""
}

bh_remote_build() {
  local commit="$1" out rc=0 t0=$SECONDS
  BH_REMOTE_UNIT="nxeon-release-build-$ENV_NAME"
  bh_ssh "systemctl is-active -q $BH_REMOTE_UNIT" </dev/null && die "a $ENV_NAME release build is already running on the build host ($BH_REMOTE_UNIT)"
  log "Building on $BUILD_HOST_NAME in nxeon-build-prod.slice (6-thread / 10 GB cap) — log there: $BH_DEPLOY_ROOT/$ENV_NAME/build.log"
  out=$(mktemp)
  # --max: the remote watchdog (BUILD_MAX_MIN) fires first; this is the backstop.
  bh_ssh "BUILD_MAX_MIN=$BUILD_MAX_MIN BUILD_STALL_MIN=$BUILD_STALL_MIN BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_SEC=$BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_SEC \
      $BH_TOOL/bin/run-capped.sh prod --unit $BH_REMOTE_UNIT --max $(( (BUILD_MAX_MIN + 40) * 60 )) \
      -- env BUILD_MAX_MIN=$BUILD_MAX_MIN BUILD_STALL_MIN=$BUILD_STALL_MIN BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_SEC=$BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_SEC \
      $BH_TOOL/bin/remote-build.sh $ENV_NAME $commit" </dev/null 2>&1 | tee "$out" | sed 's/^/    /' || true
  rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
  BH_REMOTE_UNIT=""
  REMOTE_BUILD_ID=$(grep -oE '^REMOTE_BUILD_OK BUILD_ID=[A-Za-z0-9_-]+' "$out" | tail -1 | sed 's/.*BUILD_ID=//')
  rm -f "$out"
  [ "$rc" = 0 ] && [ -n "$REMOTE_BUILD_ID" ] || die "REMOTE BUILD FAILED on $BUILD_HOST_NAME (exit $rc after $((SECONDS - t0))s) — nothing was changed here; the live app is untouched. Re-run, or --build-local to build on this box."
  log "Remote build finished in $((SECONDS - t0))s (BUILD_ID $REMOTE_BUILD_ID)"
}

# Pull the finished .next into the local build tree (delta against the previous
# build that is still there; webpack cache / trace / types stay on node-2).
bh_fetch_build() {
  local t0=$SECONDS
  log "Fetching the build from $BUILD_HOST_NAME into $BUILD_DIR/.next"
  mkdir -p "$BUILD_DIR/.next"
  rm -f "$BUILD_DIR/.next/BUILD_ID"   # a failed/partial fetch can never pass as a finished build
  local rc=0
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  timeout "$BH_RSYNC_TIMEOUT_SEC" rsync -a --delete --compress --compress-choice=zstd --timeout=120 \
    -e "ssh $BH_SSH_OPTS" --exclude=/cache --exclude=/trace --exclude=/types --exclude=/BUILD_ID \
    "$BUILD_HOST:$BH_DEPLOY_ROOT/$ENV_NAME/build/.next/" "$BUILD_DIR/.next/" </dev/null || rc=$?
  [ "$rc" = 0 ] || die "rsync of the build from $BUILD_HOST_NAME failed (exit $rc) — nothing was changed; the live app is untouched."
  # BUILD_ID last: its presence means the whole tree arrived.
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  rsync -a -e "ssh $BH_SSH_OPTS" "$BUILD_HOST:$BH_DEPLOY_ROOT/$ENV_NAME/build/.next/BUILD_ID" "$BUILD_DIR/.next/BUILD_ID" </dev/null \
    || die "could not fetch BUILD_ID"
  local got; got=$(cat "$BUILD_DIR/.next/BUILD_ID")
  [ "$got" = "$REMOTE_BUILD_ID" ] || die "fetched BUILD_ID '$got' != remote build '$REMOTE_BUILD_ID' (did another build overwrite it?)"
  # Remote and local file lists must match exactly (names + sizes).
  local lsum rsum
  lsum=$(cd "$BUILD_DIR/.next" && find . -path ./cache -prune -o -path ./trace -prune -o -path ./types -prune -o -type f -printf '%P %s\n' | sort | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
  rsum=$(bh_ssh "cd $BH_DEPLOY_ROOT/$ENV_NAME/build/.next && find . -path ./cache -prune -o -path ./trace -prune -o -path ./types -prune -o -type f -printf '%P %s\n' | sort | sha256sum | cut -c1-16" </dev/null)
  [ "$lsum" = "$rsum" ] || die "fetched build differs from the build host's (file list/size checksum $lsum != $rsum)"
  log "Fetched $(du -sh --apparent-size "$BUILD_DIR/.next" | cut -f1) in $((SECONDS - t0))s (verified: same BUILD_ID, same file list + sizes)"
}

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

content.thinking:
I'm reviewing which keys are sensitive — the Meta Conversions API token should be excluded since it's server-side only, while things like Google Ads IDs, pixel IDs, GA4 ID, and support email are public-facing and safe to include. I'm also checking table fields like HostingPlan's active status and prices, which are public info too.

Now I'm figuring out what "build snapshot" should include: an allowlisted settings table copied from prod minus the secret tokens, full HostingPlan and GamePlan tables since pricing/specs seem non-sensitive, and approved Review rows — though I need to check if reviews include reviewer emails that could be PII, since the marketing layout seems to reference an aggregate rating badge that pulls from this data.

Rather than full table copies, I'm leaning toward streaming prod data with pg_dump --data-only for HostingPlan and GamePlan into the build DB, then using psql to load it. But there's a schema-ordering risk: since schema pushes happen after the build in remote mode, prod's schema may lag the commit's schema, so a dumped COPY could fail if columns were added or removed — I'd need to handle mismatches carefully, possibly with column inserts that tolerate schema drift.

To solve this robustly, I'm thinking of computing the intersection of columns between prod and the freshly-reset node-2 schema, then doing a targeted `COPY (SELECT cols...) TO STDOUT` from prod piped into a `COPY table (cols) FROM STDIN` on node-2 — essentially building a generic snapshot function that handles arbitrary tables and WHERE clauses this way. I also need to figure out timing: the snapshot load has to happen after remote-build's schema reset step, not before, which affects where I hook this into the build sequence.

Loading approach: ship CSV snapshots to a protected directory before invoking remote-build, then after reset, load each one into a staging table with all-text columns and INSERT into the real target using only the common columns with appropriate type casts, since raw CSV column-filtering is too fragile for quoted multiline values.

Actually, a cleaner approach is exporting the snapshot as JSON lines via row_to_json, loading into a jsonb staging table, and using jsonb_populate_record to reconstruct rows into the target table automatically -- it ignores extra keys and nulls missing ones, though that could break any new NOT NULL columns without defaults.

content.thinking:
The tsc memory cap of 3072MB is causing OOM, since the full project likely needs 4-5GB. I'm considering raising NODE_OPTIONS default to 5120 and bumping the agents slice MemoryMax to 7G, which would put total parent memory around 10G, with production builds peaking near 9.8G including page cache.

The risk is that with agents running at 7G concurrently and prod anon usage around 5-6G, combined memory could exceed the 10G parent limit and trigger OOM kills since both have equal oom_score_adj. I'm weighing whether making tsc take the same build lock as prod would protect against this, though that would serialize tsc runs and create a bottleneck when many agents are active -- deciding that prod builds should get priority via MemoryLow settings on the prod slice, and checking the measured peak anon usage of the prod build slice.

I think the better fix is lowering prod's oom_score_adj to 500 versus 1000 for agents, so the memcg OOM killer's badness calculation favors killing agent processes first when memory pressure hits. For tsc memory needs, I want to actually measure peak usage rather than guess, so I'm considering temporarily raising the agents slice's MemoryMax to 7G with MemoryHigh at 6.5G and testing with a default NODE_OPTIONS heap size of 5120.

# BUILD HOST — all builds and heavy dev work run on node-2, not the primary

**Since 2026-10-07 (owner decision).** The primary (ns5002569, 51.79.162.96) only serves the live site:
prod web/worker, Postgres, customer VMs. Parallel agent builds there pushed load to 16+, filled swap
and hard-crashed it on 2026-10-06. Everything heavy now runs on **node-2 = nxeon-fsn1
(178.63.94.114)**, inside a capped systemd slice.

Full technical write-up: `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` → "Build host (node-2)".

## What runs where

| Work | Where | How |
|---|---|---|
| Production / staging release builds (`npm install`, `prisma generate`, `next build`) | node-2, `nxeon-build-prod.slice` | automatically by `scripts/promote-production.sh` / `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` |
| Schema push, pre-cutover smoke (:3095), cutover, restarts, rollback | primary | same scripts, unchanged |
| Agent `tsc`, tests, `next build`, `next dev`, Playwright, throwaway DBs | node-2, `nxeon-build-agents.slice` | `scripts/devhost` (below) |
| Editing files, git commits | primary, in **your own worktree** | as before |

## Caps on node-2 (it also runs ~13 customer VMs — never touch them)

- `nxeon.slice` CPUWeight 20 / IOWeight 10 (VMs in `qemu.slice` win any contention ~5:1)
- `nxeon-build.slice`: **CPUQuota 600 % (6 of 12 threads), MemoryMax 10 G, MemoryHigh 9.5 G, no swap**
  - `nxeon-build-prod.slice`: release builds — CPUWeight 1000, MemoryLow 6 G, oom_score_adj 500
  - `nxeon-build-agents.slice`: agent work — **MemoryMax 7 G**, oom_score_adj 1000 (dies first)
- every process: nice 10, ionice best-effort 7. Build files live on `tank` (separate SATA SSD);
  VMs are on `rpool` (NVMe), so build IO never hits their disks.
- **Build lock** on node-2: `/run/lock/nxeon-build.lock` — one heavy job at a time
  (release builds, `devhost build|test`, `devhost run --lock`). Locked agent jobs are capped at
  25 min by default so a promote (waits max 30 min) is never starved.

## How agents work from now on

1. Make your own worktree on the primary (never work in `/opt/nxeon` or `/opt/nxeon-staging`):
   `git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main`
   You do NOT need `node_modules` in it (and never symlink one in).
2. Edit with your normal tools. Then, from inside the worktree, run heavy things on node-2:
   ```
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost tsc                    # npx tsc --noEmit
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost test [test/x.test.ts]  # tsx --test (takes the build lock)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost build                  # next build (takes the build lock)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost run -- <cmd...>        # anything else; add --lock if heavy
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost db push                # schema into YOUR throwaway DB
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost dev                    # next dev on node-2 127.0.0.1:<port>
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost tunnel <port>          # reach it from the primary (curl/Playwright)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost run -- npx playwright test ...   # or run Playwright ON node-2
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost pull <path> [dest]     # copy screenshots/reports back
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost stop [name|all]        # ALWAYS stop dev servers when done
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost rm                     # when finished: units, DB and node-2 copy gone
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost status                 # node-2 load, slice memory, lock, running units
   ```
   Each command mirrors your worktree's source (git-tracked + untracked-not-ignored; never
   `.git`, `node_modules`, `.next`, `.env*`) to `/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>` on node-2, installs
   deps there when `package-lock.json`/schema changed, and runs the command in the agents slice.
   The node-2 copy is disposable — commit in your primary worktree only.
3. **Throwaway database**: every workspace gets its own `wt_<name>` on node-2's private Postgres
   cluster (`127.0.0.1:5433`, role `nxeon_agent`, never exposed). `DATABASE_URL`, a random
   `AUTH_SECRET`, `APP_URL`, `PORT` are preset. Extra non-secret env: `devhost env set K=V` (it
   refuses any value that is a live prod/staging value). **Agents never need, and must never use,
   production DB credentials.**
4. Only if node-2 is down: say so to the owner. Do not fall back to building on the primary.

## Forbidden (hard rules)

- **No `next build`, full test suites, dev servers, Playwright or JDKs on the primary.** Use devhost.
- **Never run `REASSIGN OWNED`, `DROP OWNED`, `ALTER ... OWNER`, `CREATE/ALTER/DROP ROLE`, or any
  database-ownership command** — on any cluster, including node-2's throwaway one.
- **Never `pkill`/`killall` by pattern** (`next`, `node`, `npm`, ...): it hits prod/staging too.
  Stop by unit (`devhost stop`) or by the PID on your own port.
- **Never `git add -A` / `git add .`** — add only the files you changed.
- Never touch customer VMs (`qm`, `qemu.slice`) on node-2; never raise the slice caps.
- Never copy a production `.env` (or any secret) to node-2. Never print secrets.
- Never build in `/opt/nxeon` or `/opt/nxeon-staging`; never `git checkout` there.

## Deploys (owner/root only)

`scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` — unchanged usage;
the build now happens on node-2 automatically. `--build-local` = emergency fallback (old on-box
build) if node-2 is unreachable. Rollback unchanged: `scripts/rollback-release.sh --production`.

## Admin

- Re-provision / refresh node-2 (idempotent): `scripts/buildhost/provision.sh` (ships the
  primary's exact Node toolchain to `/opt/nxeon-build/node`, re-applies slices, datasets, mirror,
  Postgres). Run it after upgrading Node on the primary — promotes refuse a version mismatch.
- Release build log on node-2: `/tank/nxeon-deploy/<env>/build.log`.

More importantly, other running agent sessions are still building on the primary until told otherwise, so the parent should broadcast the BUILD-HOST.md guidance, and I'm considering whether a guard against live-tree builds should be extended further.

## Build host on node-2: done, and a real production promote went through it successfully

Production and staging builds, and all agent dev work, now run on node-2 (nxeon-fsn1). The primary only serves the live site.

### What runs where now
- **On node-2** (inside a capped slice): `npm install`, `prisma generate` and `next build` for the exact commit being promoted. Also all agent tsc, tests, builds, dev servers, Playwright and throwaway databases.
- **On the primary**: checking out the commit (needed for the schema, `public/` and geoip data), a light `npm install` so it has the Prisma CLI, `prisma db push`, putting the real `.env` into the build, staging the release, the smoke test on :3095, the symlink cutover, restarts, the worker, pruning and rollback.
- **One ordering change**: the schema push now runs after the remote build (it used to run before). The remote build never touches the database, and the smoke test is the first step that needs the new schema.
- **`--build-local`** on both `promote-production.sh` and `deploy-staging.sh` falls back to the old on-box build, in the old order.
- **Release history**: `release.json` now records `"builtOn":"nxeon-fsn1"`.

### Caps on node-2
- **Top level**: `nxeon.slice` has CPUWeight 20 and IOWeight 10. Customer VMs in `qemu.slice` are at 100, so under contention they get about 5 times more.
- **`nxeon-build.slice`**: CPUQuota 600% (6 of 12 threads), MemoryMax 10G, MemoryHigh 9.5G, no swap.
- **Release builds** run in `nxeon-build-prod.slice`: CPUWeight 1000, MemoryLow 6G, OOM score 500.
- **Agent work** runs in `nxeon-build-agents.slice`: MemoryMax 7G, OOM score 1000. Inside the cap an agent process gets killed before a release build, and both die before any VM if node-2 runs out of memory.
- **Every process** runs at nice 10, ionice best-effort 7.
- **Disks**: all build data is on `tank` (a separate SATA SSD), with ZFS quotas: 300G for `tank/nxeon-build`, 80G for `tank/nxeon-deploy`. The VMs are on rpool (NVMe), so build IO never touches their disks.
- **Build lock**: node-2 has its own `/run/lock/nxeon-build.lock`. A promote waits up to 30 minutes for it, and locked agent jobs stop after 25 minutes by default, so a promote is never starved.
- **Node version**: Node v22.23.1 and npm 10.9.8 are copied from the primary's own install into `/opt/nxeon-build/node`. node-2's own Node v24 is untouched. A promote refuses to run if the two versions differ.
- **Compiler**: I installed `g++` and `make` on node-2. The ssh2 and cpu-features native addons are compiled at install time; production has always shipped them, and without a compiler node-2's output would quietly differ.
- **Customer VMs** were not touched.

### Build-time env: what node-2 gets and why
The production `.env` is not copied to node-2. What the build actually needs:
- **Env values**: there are no `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` keys, middleware reads its env at runtime, and only 5 routes are prerendered (`/robots.txt`, `/locations`, the manifest, the OG image, the icon). So node-2 gets only `APP_URL`, plus `NXEON_SANDBOX` for staging. The file is regenerated from the live `.env` on every build and stored root-only, mode 600, at `/etc/nxeon-build/<env>.build.env`.
- **The build also needs a database:**
  - `/mods/games/[family]` runs a catalogue query at build time, and the build fails if no database answers.
  - While `/locations` is prerendered, the layouts read settings and HostingPlan prices, and those get baked into the page. That covers the Meta domain-verification tag, the hosting promo banner and the footer social links.
- **How that's handled**: node-2 gets an empty database on its own private Postgres (127.0.0.1:5433). It is reset to the commit's schema on every build and loaded with a small public snapshot:
  - the HostingPlan table (3 rows);
  - 41 allow-listed Setting keys (18 of them currently have values), excluding secrets like `meta_capi_token`.

  Every value in that snapshot is already shown in public HTML. No secret and no production database URL leaves the primary.
- **Verified on the same commit:**
  - Scanning both builds for every prod `.env` value gives identical hit counts. Those hits are values that also appear as literals in the source; no secret appears in either output.
  - `/locations` from node-2 has the same content as the primary's build. The other 4 prerendered files are byte-identical.
  - Without the snapshot, `/locations` lost the verification tag, the banner and the social links. That is why it exists.
- **Ongoing check**: each build reports any Setting key it read that isn't in the snapshot. If a new static page starts rendering a new setting, add it to `BUILD_SNAPSHOT_SETTING_KEYS`.

### The proof deploy
- **Pre-checks**: the deploy queue was idle and main was at 58f967d0. I dry-ran production and staging through the new path first; both passed, including the pre-cutover smoke test.
- **Merge**: I fast-forwarded main to 109e4a134e (scripts and docs only, no app code) and ran `bash scripts/promote-production.sh` from `/opt/nxeon`.
- **Result**: exit 0. Live release is `20261007T162846Z-109e4a13-o6ywS0e1QDdBvsif0k3Sb`, built on nxeon-fsn1. The schema was already in sync.
- **Health checks**: smoke test and cutover checks all returned 200. nxeon-web and nxeon-worker are both active.
- **Public site**: `/`, `/login`, `/locations`, `/robots.txt` and `/pricing` all return 200. `/locations` shows the new build ID, the verification tag, the banner and the social links.
- **Rollback**: not needed.

| | Primary (on-box builds) | node-2 (this deploy) |
|---|---|---|
| `next build` | 541–828s (promotes b3–b10, e.g. 707s and 631s for the last two) | 270–286s |
| Whole remote step | n/a | about 300s (+20s when dependencies change) |
| Fetching the build back | n/a | 78–98s (about 7 MB/s, 185 ms latency) |
| Total promote | 748–1077s (845s for b10) | 695s |

- **Primary load during the build**: between 4.5 and 7.8, below its baseline of about 9 from other activity. During the b10 on-box build it was about 13.
- **node-2 during the build**: load 2–3.5, available memory never below about 10.7 GB, no out-of-memory events. Peak memory in the build slice was 9.4 GB including file cache.
- **Cold restart**: still about 118s until healthy, same as before this change.

### How agents work from now on
Rules are in `/root/agent-notes/BUILD-HOST.md`; read it before running anything heavy.
1. Each agent makes its own worktree on the primary and edits there with normal tools. It needs no `node_modules`.
2. Heavy work goes through `/opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost` (`tsc`, `test`, `build`, `run [--lock] -- cmd`, `db push`, `dev`, `tunnel`, `pull`, `stop`, `rm`, `status`).
3. devhost copies the worktree's source to node-2 (never `.git`, `node_modules`, `.next` or `.env*`) and runs the command in the agents slice.
4. Each workspace gets its own throwaway database (`wt_<name>`) on 127.0.0.1:5433, which is never exposed. `devhost env set` refuses any value that is live on prod or staging, so agents never need production credentials.
5. **Tested**:
   - full-app `tsc` passed in 1m48s;
   - `db push`;
   - `next dev` with `/login` returning 200 on node-2 and through the tunnel;
   - a test file run with the lock;
   - `rm`.

   Playwright browsers and libraries were already on node-2 but I didn't run a Playwright test.
6. The rules doc also covers the forbidden commands: no REASSIGN/DROP OWNED or any role/database-ownership command, no pkill by pattern, no `git add -A`, no builds or dev servers on the primary, no prod secrets on node-2.

### Things the owner may want to do
- **Tell running agent sessions.** Sessions already in progress don't know about this yet. Nothing technically stops a `next build` on the primary outside the live trees. A follow-up could make `npm run build` refuse on the primary unless `--build-local` is set.
- **Push to GitHub if wanted.** `infra/build-on-node2` and the new main (109e4a134e) are local only; I didn't push them to GitHub.
- **After any Node upgrade on the primary**, run `scripts/buildhost/provision.sh`. Promotes refuse to run on a version mismatch. The same script re-provisions node-2 if anything there is lost.
- **Two staged-but-never-deployed releases from my dry-runs** are kept for inspection: production `20261007T160033Z-…` and staging `20261007T161142Z-…`. Normal pruning removes them, nothing to do.
- **The memory index has no entry for this yet.** A note pointing to BUILD-HOST.md and the docs section is worth adding.

### Files
- New: `scripts/devhost`, `scripts/lib/buildhost.sh`, `scripts/lib/buildhost-env.sh`, `scripts/buildhost/{provision,setup-node2,remote-build,run-capped}.sh`
- Changed: `scripts/lib/seamless-release.sh`, `scripts/promote-production.sh`, `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` (all under `/opt/nxeon`)
- Docs: `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` section "Build host (node-2) — release builds and agent dev work off the primary", plus a changelog entry; `/root/agent-notes/BUILD-HOST.md`
- Proof deploy logs: `/root/promote-buildhost.log` and `/root/promote-buildhost-load.log`
- On node-2:
  - `/opt/nxeon-build/{node,bin}`
  - `/tank/nxeon-build`, `/tank/nxeon-deploy`
  - `/etc/nxeon-build/`
  - the `nxeon*.slice` units
  - `postgresql@17-agents`
